#1943. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his new-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

Just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys

Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti

Richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and new signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

He fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Important defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR says the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH

This has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Important block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

This is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

The new man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being new signings] I have a big confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a big personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an important player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an important team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at new signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

There will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

#1942. Borussia Dortmund vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 16:17, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:15

BVB Stadion will play host to an intriguing Champions League fixture on Wednesday evening, as Borussia Dortmund welcome Real Betis.

Dortmund are 13th in the Champions League league stage table, picking up six points from three matches, while Betis are fifth in the rankings on nine points.

Dortmund opened their 2026-27 Champions League league stage campaign with a 3-2 home success over Villarreal, before suffering a 1-0 defeat to Bodo/Glimt in their second match, but they returned to winning ways last time out, beating Sabah 2-1.

A return of six points from three matches has left BVB in 13th spot in the overall table, and they will bring a five-game unbeaten run into this contest, including a 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga on Saturday night.

Dortmund, who have won three of their last four matches during a strong run, are preparing to face Real Betis for the first time, but they have won each of their last four UEFA matches against Spanish opposition, all of which have been at home.

Niko Kovac's side will follow this match with back-to-back Bundesliga games against Elversberg and Borussia Monchengladbach, before returning to European action against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on November 24.

Dortmund reached the Champions League knockout phase playoffs in 2025-26, losing to Atalanta BC, so there is plenty of room for improvement this term.

Real Betis, meanwhile, will enter the match off the back of a 2-1 win over Malaga in La Liga, with the result leaving them fourth in their domestic table.

It has been a strong start to the 2026-27 campaign for Manuel Pellegrini's side, who have been victorious in their opening three matches of this season's Champions League.

The Seville outfit started their European campaign with a 3-2 victory over Lille, before posting a 3-2 win over Porto; six points then became nine courtesy of a 1-0 success over Feyenoord, and they are up in fifth spot in the overall table.

Real Betis reached the quarter-finals of the 2025-26 Europa League, losing to Braga, while they were in the final of the 2024-25 Conference League, being beaten by Chelsea.

El Glorioso last competed in the Champions League in 2005-06, being knocked out in the group stage, but they look capable of advancing to the knockout round of this season's European Cup.

Borussia Dortmund form (all competitions):

Dortmund will be without the services of Kaua Prates (muscle), but the home side are otherwise in strong form for their clash with Real Betis.

Serhou Guirassy has been in strong form this season, scoring eight times and registering two assists in 13 appearances, and the 30-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

Fabio Silva has five goals and two assists in 13 matches this season and will also start, while Jobe Bellingham is in line to feature as an advanced midfielder for the German club.

As for Real Betis, Cucho Hernandez (calf) and Junior Firpo (muscular) are both out of the match, but no fresh issues have been reported.

Three players have scored four times for Real Betis this season - Isco, Marc Bartra and Abde Ezzalzouli - and the trio are set to feature in the first XI.

Troy Parrott has two goals in 11 appearances for the Seville outfit during the 2026-27 campaign and should also feature in the starting side due to Hernandez's absence.

Meanwhile, Antony and Pablo Fornals are expected to be in the XI.

Borussia Dortmund possible starting lineup:

Kobel; Gadou, Anton, Schlotterbeck; Ryerson, Veerman, Nmecha, Svensson; Bellingham; F Silva, Guirassy

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, F Garcia; Fornals, Roca; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Parrott

Real Betis have been excellent in this season's Champions League, and the La Liga club deserve a lot of respect, but Dortmund at home are a tough proposition, and we are backing BVB to edge a close game on Wednesday.

#1939. Why West Ham fans should welcome - and be wary of - Scott Parker appointment

Scott Parker is the frontrunner to succeed Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked as West Ham head coach on Tuesday morning with the club’s promotion hopes hanging in the balance.

West Ham were widely considered favourites to bounce straight back to the Premier League this season, but after six wins from their first 13 Championship games, they are down in eighth place.

Having recorded a £104.2million loss in the last financial year, the club are acutely aware of the financial imperative of returning to the top flight at the first opportunity and have moved swiftly to make a change in the dugout following successive home defeats to Southampton and West Brom.

Parker, a club legend who won three successive Player of the Year awards during a four-year stint in east London, is seen as someone who can not only get supporters back onside but has experience getting teams promoted from the Championship.

The 46-year-old has earned promotion to the Premier League on three separate occasions across spells with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, but his success has not come without criticism.

His time at Fulham, who offered him his first senior managerial role in May 2019, was dominated by tensions with the board, and Parker openly criticised the club’s long-term structure and recruitment.

West Ham agree new manager appointment after Nuno sacking

West Ham confirm Nuno Espirito Santo sack decision as statement issued

Nuno under pressure as West Ham sent tumbling down Championship table

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Despite taking Fulham up from the Championship, Parker then struggled to build a competitive Premier League side and presided over a dispiriting relegation campaign, with his pragmatic style of play proving increasingly unpopular with supporters.

Parker left Fulham by mutual consent after their relegation in 2021 before swiftly taking charge at Bournemouth. While not direct rivals, the move left a bitter taste for some, with Bournemouth in direct competition with Fulham for promotion from the Championship.

Both teams went up automatically during the 2021/22 season. But while Fulham were able to stabilise under the guidance of Marco Silva, similar issues reared their head for Parker, and he was sacked four games into the season after questioning the direction and commitment of the club following a 9-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Parker’s comments, in which he said his team were "ill-equipped at this level", led Bournemouth’s then-owner Maxim Demin to hit back, stating that for the club to progress, everyone must “show belief in and respect for one another.”

Scott Parker is a manager with pedigree at this level but also plenty of baggage

West Ham will be aware of Parker’s history, including an ill-fated 67-day spell at Belgian side Club Brugge, and they will have made it clear during negotiations that he must secure promotion to secure his future.

After a toxic end to Nuno’s tenure, there will be a fair amount of goodwill for the former England international given his cult status at the club and his knowledge of the league.

The Championship is relentless, though, and results need to change quickly if West Ham are to keep pace with the top of the table and stop the chasing pack from gaining encouragement.

In Parker, West Ham believe they have a safe pair of hands who knows the club and knows how to get out of the Championship. Supporters are, however, bound to be more sceptical.

Parker’s vision for West Ham will almost certainly be built on defensive solidity, and with good reason. West Ham have conceded 18 goals in 13 league games this season, a rate of 1.4 goals per game.

Given the quality of the squad at his disposal, though, there will also be an expectation to entertain. West Ham, for all their struggles, have at times blown teams away this season, scoring in every game this term.

Parker is a manager with pedigree at this level but also plenty of baggage. West Ham can’t say they have not been warned.

#1938. Man United news: Erik ten Hag says relegation "is possible" amid Michael Carrick struggles

By Darren Plant | 02 Nov 2026 16:20

Erik ten Hag has claimed that former club Manchester United cannot rely on reputation alone to avoid relegation from the Premier League.

Man United are currently preparing to face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night having not won a game in any competition since September 10.

Although Michael Carrick was defiant in a press conference on Monday, the Red Devils only sit outside of the Premier League relegation zone on goal difference.

Given the players that they have at their disposal and the increasing possibility of appointing a more experienced replacement for Carrick, the assumption is that Man United will retain their top-flight status.

Nevertheless, speaking to ESPN NL's 'Goedemorgen Eredivisie', Ten Hag says that no-one associated with Man United can afford any complacency.

The Dutchman claims that Man United are at risk of being involved in a "vicious circle".

He said: "In the Premier League it's certainly possible, because all the teams are simply strong.

"They're all strong squads, all good managers. And if you end up on the wrong side once and you really get into that vicious circle, then it can become very difficult."

Man United have not suffered relegation from the top flight of English football since 1974.

Of 12 managers who have been in the Man United dugout since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement, only three have lifted silverware.

With a Europa League, League Cup and Community Shield to his name and a win ratio of more than 58% over 144 matches, the stats say that Jose Mourinho is Man United's best manager since Ferguson.

While Ten Hag never had the same affinity with the fans as the Portuguese, he guided the club to a League Cup and FA Cup across a 128-game stint.

Despite his reputation having lowered from his time at Old Trafford, Ten Hag deserves more respect for the job that he did at the Theatre of Dreams.

#1934. Porto vs Napoli - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 02 Nov 2026 17:13, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 13:42

One of three teams still without a point, Porto will again try to get off the mark in this season's Champions League when Napoli visit Estadio do Dragao on Wednesday evening.

While the Italian side got up and running last time out, they have lost six and won none of their last seven away games at Europe's top level.

Last month's 1-0 home loss to PSV Eindhoven was Porto's third consecutive Champions League defeat, leaving them in danger of failing to make the knockout rounds later this term.

Following previous setbacks against Manchester City and Real Betis, the Dragons have crucially conceded the first goal each time, always putting them on the back foot.

So, approaching the midpoint of this season's league phase, Porto need at least nine points just to reach the playoffs - and that may not even prove enough.

Still facing tough trips to Feyenoord and Liverpool, Francesco Farioli's men must try to maximise home advantage in midweek, having continued their domestic domination last time out.

After ending a three-year wait for the Portuguese title, they have brought that form into the current campaign: 10 straight wins have put them well clear of both Lisbon clubs atop the Primeira Liga table.

Keeping yet another clean sheet, Porto strolled to a 4-0 win against rock-bottom Estoril at the weekend, and they have only conceded four goals so far.

However, they are now expected to make more of an impact in Europe, as the former Champions League winners look to regain lost glories.

When Farioli hosts his fellow Tuscan Massimiliano Allegri on Wednesday, it will mark the fifth competitive meeting between Porto and Napoli.

In a couple of two-legged ties, each side has gone through once: the Italian side progressed in the 1974-75 UEFA Cup, and Porto won 3-2 on aggregate in the 2013-14 Europa League.

This time, Napoli are three points ahead of their Portuguese counterparts in the Champions League, after edging a chaotic seven-goal contest against Bodo/Glimt on matchday three.

Having lost to Arsenal and Villarreal before welcoming the Norwegian giant-killers to Campania, they finally posted the club's 100th win in UEFA competition, largely thanks to Scott McTominay's brace.

Yet, before setting off for northern Portugal, Napoli are winless in seven Champions League away games, which partly explains why they finished 30th in the 36-team table last term.

A former finalist with Juventus, Allegri has personally lost eight of his last 10 matches at the elite level, and he is also under pressure for some dismal domestic results.

After his current team lost 2-0 to Juve on Sunday evening, they lie eighth in the Serie A standings and - with a 14-point deficit to surprise leaders Lazio - are surely already out of the title race.

Porto are still missing injured pair William Gomes and Vasco Sousa, while it remains to be seen if Polish winger Oskar Pietuszewski will be ready to play in midweek.

The latter skipped Saturday's league fixture with a minor thigh problem, while left-back Zaidu limped off at half time due to a knee issue.

Martim Fernandes missed that game with tonsillitis but could be involved on Wednesday; Chris Smalling, Gabriel Mec and Dominik Prpic will not, having been left off Farioli's Champions League list.

Allegri's options have been trimmed by a number of absences: Alessandro Buongiorno, David Neres, Costantino Favasuli, Alisson Santos, Leonardo Spinazzola and Benoit Badiashile were already unavailable before Stanislav Lobotka injured his left ankle last week.

Vanja-Milinkovic Savic also missed the defeat to Juventus with a knock, and first-choice striker Rasmus Hojlund was sidelined by flu.

Furthermore, full-backs Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Mathias Olivera both sustained muscular injuries in Turin.

Despite a slight ankle sprain, Kevin De Bruyne may make his 86th Champions League appearance from the bench: the Belgian veteran has already created 10 chances from open play in this season's edition.

#1933. Where to watch Manchester United vs Roma: TV channel and live stream for Champions League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Manchester United host Roma in the Champions League tonight as Michael Carrick desperately seeks an end to their woeful winless run.

The beleaguered Man Utd boss may now have only two games left to save his job, with a further review expected during the November international break, following Sunday’s home clash with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

Though his side delivered a much-improved first-half display against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, the wheels then swiftly fell off in familiarly chaotic fashion as Lisandro Martinez was dismissed in a 2-0 loss - United’s third in a row and fourth in the last five matches.

They have gone nine matches without a victory for the first time since the 1988/89 season to spark genuine concern over a potential relegation battle, having not won at all since their last Champions League home fixture - the 4-0 drubbing of Azerbaijani debutants Sabah FK on September 10.

But, having lost away at Atletico Madrid and Como since then to slip to 21st in the league phase table, they can expect a much sterner challenge from Roma, who continue to thrive despite a lengthy injury list that has seen them travel to Old Trafford with only 17 available outfield players.

The Giallorossi are in strong form under Gian Piero Gasperini and sit third in Serie A, still unbeaten and four points adrift of leaders Inter Milan after 10 games having won four of their last five matches across all competitions including Saturday’s 5-2 demolition of struggling Udinese.

Roma brushed aside Slovan Bratislava 4-0 in their last Champions League outing, having also been edged out by Real Madrid in a seven-goal thriller and drawn with Fenerbahce to sit 15th.

Carrick will hope to invoke the spirit of 2007, when he scored twice for United in a memorable 7-1 home trouncing of Roma in the Champions League quarter-finals.

TV channel and live stream: Unlike most Champions League fixtures, tonight’s game is not being shown live in the UK on TNT Sports.

Instead, it will be broadcast by Amazon Prime Video, who still have the first pick of one Tuesday night match up until the semi-finals.

Coverage begins at 6:30pm GMT ahead of an 8pm kick-off at Old Trafford, presented by Gabby Logan and featuring punditry from former Man United trio Wayne Rooney, Nicky Butt and Ashley Young.

#1932. Crystal Palace make decision over Jean-Philippe Mateta red card appeal before Liverpool

Crystal Palace have lodged an appeal against the red card awarded to Jean-Philippe Mateta during their 2-0 defeat to Tottenham last Saturday.

Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, following a VAR review, for a studs-up challenge on Micky van de Ven as the pair contested for a loose ball at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Referee Michael Oliver originally awarded Mateta a yellow card but upgraded his decision after being sent to the monitor to have a second look at the challenge.

With Palace down to 10 men, Spurs took control of the game and sealed a comfortable victory after goals in either half from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke.

Mateta landed on top of Van de Ven’s right ankle with his studs up as he chased a pass into space, and Oliver deemed the 29-year-old to have used “full forceful contact” as he explained his decision inside the stadium.

Palace’s view, though, is that Mateta’s challenge was accidental, and they argue that the French international had his eyes on the ball and did not see Van de Ven coming.

Mateta currently faces a three-match suspension, but Palace hope the decision is either overturned or his ban reduced.

Pierre Sage, who is under increasing pressure to turn things around at Palace, has only recently welcomed Mateta back into the fold after a hamstring injury and will desperately want his star striker back available.

If Mateta’s ban is upheld, he would miss this weekend’s home game against Liverpool, as well as crunch fixtures against newly promoted teams Coventry and Hull.

He will, however, be available for selection when Palace host Hoffenheim and Real Sociedad in the Europa League.

#1931. RB Leipzig vs Manchester City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 18:00, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 12:49

Former Manchester City defender Martin Demichelis will lead his RB Leipzig side into Wednesday night’s Champions League clash with the Citizens at the Red Bull Arena.

The two teams butt heads for the first time since November 2023 when City came from two goals down at half time to win 3-2 in a thrilling group-stage contest at the Etihad Stadium.

Just three days after edging past Brighton & Hove Albion on penalties in the EFL Cup fourth round, Man City delivered a surprisingly toothless display against the same opponent last Saturday as they fell to a narrow 1-0 home defeat in the Premier League.

For the third time this season, Enzo Maresca’s side conceded inside the opening 15 minutes, with Yasin Ayari’s goal enough to condemn the Citizens to back-to-back Premier League losses as well as surrender top spot to champions Arsenal.

City will be desperate to return to winning ways in their next top-flight fixture at Nottingham Forest prior to November’s international break, but they must first shift their attention to the Champions League where they have accumulated six points from their opening three League Phase fixtures.

Sitting 10th in the 36-team standings, the Sky Blues suffered a 4-2 home defeat to holders Paris Saint-Germain in between victories against Porto (2-0) and AEK Athens (5-1), beating the latter with a much-changed side a fortnight ago.

Man City have come out on top in only eight of their last 20 Champions League matches (D2 L10), but they head to Germany having won four of their previous six meetings with Leipzig (D1 L1) while they have also prevailed in 21 of their 32 UCL encounters against German opposition (D5 L6).

After a season without European competition, RB Leipzig are back in the Champions League this term and have picked up just three points from their first three matches, leaving them down in 29th place in the 36-team League Phase table.

Die Roten Bullen edged to a slender 1-0 home win over Dutch champions PSV Eindhoven on matchday two, courtesy of a late goal from Brajan Gruda, but this result took place in between heavy 4-1 away defeats to both Como and Real Madrid.

Appointed head coach in June, Martin Demichelis has won eight and lost five of his 13 matches in charge of Leipzig in all competitions; they beat Schalke 04 by a 2-0 scoreline last Saturday to climb up to fourth in the Bundesliga standings, just three points behind unbeaten leaders Bayern Munich.

Demichelis made 15 appearances for Wednesday’s opponents Man City in the Champions League between 2013-14 and 2015-16, with the former Argentine defender scoring once in a 2-1 win away against Borussia Monchengladbach in September 2015.

The 45-year-old is now aiming to steer his Leipzig side to their fourth consecutive victory in all competitions and their first over Man City since they celebrated a 2-1 home triumph in the 2021-22 group stage. However, Die Roten Bullen have lost their last five UEFA games against English opposition.

RB Leipzig duo Assan Ouedraogo (shoulder) and Marc Guiu (muscle) remain sidelined with injuries, while former Burnley defender Maxime Esteve is doubtful with a knock that forced him to miss last weekend’s win over Schalke.

Christopher Nkunku watched on as an unused substitute last time out and it remains to be seen whether he will be fit to start on Wednesday; the Frenchman is one of only five UCL players to score a hat-trick and finish on the losing team, with his memorable treble coming in a 6-3 defeat at Man City in 2021-22.

Antonio Nusa, who has scored a team-high five goals this season, could start on the left side of front three next to Gruda and Romulo Cardoso, while Christoph Baumgartner may be fit to start in centre-midfield at the expense of Rocco Reitz.

As for Man City, their only injury concern is with attacker Antoine Semenyo, who will likely target a return from a knee injury in mid-December.

Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden are two strong contenders to earn a recall, the latter of whom score a hat-trick in City’s convincing win over AEK Athens. At least one of Ayyoub Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez or Elliot Anderson could therefore make way.

Marc Guehi is pushing to start at centre-back alongside either Abdukodir Khusanov or Ruben Dias, while Josko Gvardiol – who scored for Leipzig against Man City in the first leg of a last-16 tie in the 2022-23 Champions League – could be replaced at left-back by Nico O'Reilly.

Erling Haaland has scored more goals against Leipzig (12 goals, eight games) than against any other opponent in his career, including a UCL record-equalling five strikes in City's 7-0 win in the second leg of the last-16 tie in 2022-23. Few would be surprised to see the prolific Norwegian start again on Wednesday.

Vandevoordt; Baku, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; Banzuzi, El Aynaoui, Baumgartner; Gruda, Romulo, Nusa

Manchester City possible starting lineup:

Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi, O'Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Foden, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

The previous six meetings between Leipzig and Man City have produced 30 goals – an average of five per game – so an entertaining, end-to-end encounter can be expected on Wednesday.

The Citizens have conceded 12 goals in their last six matches and continue to look vulnerable at the back, providing Leipzig with plenty of optimism. However, we are backing Maresca’s men to rediscover their clinical touch and outscore their German counterparts in a six-goals thriller.

#1930. Liverpool confirm Ryan Gravenberch injury blow as Andoni Iraola names squad for Champions League clash

Liverpool have been dealt a new injury blow as Ryan Gravenberch will miss the Champions League showdown against Fenerbahce.

Gravenberch has cemented himself as a regular in Liverpool’s midfield since the autumn international break, starting five of the seven matches across all competitions.

He did, however, miss the comeback win over Brentford through suspension after being sent off in the defeat to Manchester City and was then dropped for the 1-0 loss to Arsenal at the weekend.

Gravenberch was expected to be in contention for Liverpool against Fenerbahce on Wednesday, but it has since been revealed that the Dutchman will not be making the trip to Turkey.

A Liverpool statement reads: “A heel injury means the midfielder will not be part of the Reds’ travelling squad for Wednesday’s meeting with the Turkish side in Istanbul.

“He will instead remain at the AXA Training Centre to undergo treatment with the club’s medical team.”

As such, Gravenberch joins Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and fellow Dutchman Jeremie Frimpong as the five Liverpool injury absentees against Fenerbahce.

Iraola issued an update on the Dutchman on Tuesday: "It is a day to day thing.

“The fracture healed, it is about the pain. He has some discomfort. It is going to be something every day we will ask him how he is."

Wataru Endo and Federico Chiesa, meanwhile, are unavailable due to not being named in the club’s squad list for the Champions League this season.

It remains to be seen if Gravenberch will be fit to face Crystal Palace at the weekend, though he has a battle on his hands to regain a midfield spot from Trey Nyoni.

“The thinking is that he's playing very well and we trust him," Iraola told Sky Sports pre-match of his decision to drop Gravenberch in favour of Nyoni against Arsenal.

#1929. AC Milan 3-1 Inter: Moreira inspires commanding fourth straight derby win

AC Milan recorded a huge win in the derby against Inter, scoring three times in the first half to secure a 3-1 win.

It did not take long for Milan to go in front, with Christian Pulisic heading in a cross from Diego Moreira. Then, just a few minutes later, Adrien Rabiot was on hand to fire in a corner first time and make it a two-goal lead.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Alessandro Bastoni scored from a corner to make it a one-goal lead once again, but then Moreira’s free-kick re-established the two-goal lead and that would be enough to see the Rossoneri through to the end of the game.

It marked a fourth straight win for Milan in the derby and it reduces the gap to the city rivals back down to four points.

Ruben Amorim chose to make six changes from the team that lost to Bologna on Wednesday night, with Mario Gila, Sankhoun Diawara, Luka Modric, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all getting the nod.

Inside four minutes, Milan took the lead and it was the derby talisman Christian Pulisic who struck once again. It was quite a simple move down the right side in the end, with Diego Moreira checking back inside onto his left foot and whipped in a simply perfect cross for Pulisic to nod in from a few yards out.

Then, just a few minutes later, Milan doubled their advantage from a set-piece after another good spell of pressure. A low delivery from Moreira found the run of Rabiot towards the near post, who somehow managed to divert it in via the far post to make it 2-0.

Midway through the first half, Inter got themselves back into the game through a dead ball of their own. A corner was flicked on at the near post towards Bastoni, who was on hand to nod in from a few yards with the Milan defenders rooted.

Inter assumed the ascendancy after the goal, and they twice threatened in quick succession shortly after their first goal. Calhanoglu had a shot tipped over from the edge of the box, then another flicked header from a corner drew a desperate reaction save from Maignan.

Milan continued to give their city rivals opportunities to try and make it a brand new game. A silly foul by Pavlovic on Spence drew a free-kick just off the right edge of the box, though the eventual shot from Diouf was grasped by Maignan.

Just over 10 minutes before the break, Inter had another chance to draw themselves level. A cross from the left was not cut out by Koni De Winter, and the ball fells to Spence who fired with his left foot, but the Frenchman makes a brilliant reaction save to deflect the shot out for a corner.

Just two minutes before the break, Milan restored their two-goal advantage thanks to a quite simply beautiful free-kick from Diego Moreira. After getting two assists to his name already on the night, he turned scorer with a fantastic attempt that was up and over the wall, dipping just enough to land inside the near right post.

Ten minutes into the second half, Inter had the first big opening and it fell to their recent danger man Carlos Augusto. A cross to the far post wasn’t tracked by anyone and the wing-back ghosted in at the far post, heading it wide from about a yard off the ground.

With 25 minutes left, a corner this time for Milan: Modric’s cross from the left finds Rabiot at the near post, who tries to head it in, but his connection was poor and the ball went straight out.

In the 75th minute, it looked like the game was going to be on once again when the referee gave a penalty for what he adjudged to be a handball on Mario Gila. The replays show that the cross struck his midriff, and therefore the penalty was overturned to be a corner.

With the game settled into a rhythm of attack versus defence, Amorim chose to make a double change with eight minutes to go. Pulisic and Diawara were the ones who came off, with Alphadjo Cisse and Davide Bartesaghi the ones to come on.

In the penultimate minute of added time, a double sub came from Amorim. Ramos and Moreira came off, Filippo Terracciano and Omari Hutchinson came on.

Alphadjo Cisse came on inside the final minutes and immediately came close to scoring. The Italian forward tried a curling shot from outside the area, but Martinez saved well to put it out for a corner, keeping it 3-1.

#1928. Alan Shearer makes Arsenal claim after win over Liverpool

Alan Shearer hailed Arsenal’s defence as the ‘best in world football’ after a hard-fought win over Liverpool.

The reigning champions moved to the top of the Premier League with a 1-0 victory at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

Kai Havertz gave Arsenal the lead on 16 minutes and that proved to be enough to bag all three points despite some intense Liverpool pressure.

While Liverpool mounted attack after attack, they mustered just one shot on target against an Arsenal side who have conceded just 10 goals in 15 games this season.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘That is how you work as a team,’ Shearer told Premier League Productions after Arsenal’s first win at Anfield in 14 years. ‘That is how you defend as a team.

‘Every single one of them to a man were outstanding. When they were under the cosh in the second half, you could see how much they wanted to defend and what it means to them to keep a clean sheet.

‘I don’t think there is a better team in world football that defend quite like Arsenal defend. Every player does their bit, it isn’t just the back four.

‘It was brilliant sitting behind the Arsenal bench today and seeing what it means to them. The team ethic and team work and belief Arteta has in them.

‘He didn’t get flustered at all even when Arsenal had to suffer. He trusts his players.’

Former Arsenal winger Theo Walcott also heaped praise on the Gunners’ defence, insisting that solidity will make Mikel Arteta’s side ‘difficult to stop this year’.

‘Arsenal frustrated them,’ Walcott said. ‘To limit Liverpool to no shots on target shows the level of this team. They just love defending, don’t they?

‘I felt like they don’t mind that pressure. These are champions who can do a bit of everything. They are going to be difficult to stop this year.

‘I look at Arsenal’s forward players and at no point do they get frustrated working for the team. That is different to many years ago.

#1927. Dwight Yorke names the manager Manchester United must appoint to replace Michael Carrick

Manchester United hero Dwight Yorke has told the Red Devils to pay whatever is necessary to bring in Unai Emery as manager.

Michael Carrick remains in charge at Old Trafford, but after nine games without a win his grip on the job looks very flimsy.

United have two games before the next international break, hosting Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and then Emery’s Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday.

If they win neither of those contests then it seems extremely difficult to imagine Carrick will still be in charge when the players return from international duty.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Yorke, who played for Villa from 1989-98 before moving to Manchester United, says Emery is the only man for the job and the Red Devils should have done whatever they could to get him before they hired Ruben Amorim in 2024 and should do the same now.

‘I have said this all along, and it baffles me when people are now jumping on the bandwagon,’ Yorke said on talkSPORT.

‘I said this two-and-a-half years ago. Unai Emery was the man to go and get way before Amorim has come into the equation.

‘And just like how, you go and spend £70million on players, I think Unai Emery, you can go and spend that money, I am not saying £70m, but pay whatever Villa has asked and get him. Give him the authority to come in.

‘I have said that way before Amorim has come in. I got a backlash from the Villa fans, and to this day, I still believe that he is the best manager in the business, certainly to get Man Utd to some type of credibility and sustainability at the same time as well.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Yorke recognises that the Manchester United players are massively under-performing, but feels that Carrick has to take some of the blame for that as he appears unable to turn the tide.

‘When things are good, which it was really good under Carrick when he first took over, football is easy,’ said the former striker.

‘The difference in management is when things are not so good. As a player when things are not so good, have you got the character to bounce back?

‘This is where we have seen Carrick is being let down. You need a reaction from your players. Whether the players are on board with you, are they going to fight for you? I’ve not seen that.

‘We’ve seen Carrick in his element when things are really good. When things have not gone so well the manager’s job is trying to motivate the players, get them back to playing, showing some character, play with conviction, play with passion.

‘Even if you lose a football match, that’s fine. But if you lose football matches the way United have been losing football matches, I’m afraid that it does not look good.

‘You look at Tottenham, for instance, they were at the bottom and the manager somehow finds a way. You’ve got to find a way from your players and I’m not seeing that with Carrick.

‘This is the time as a manager when you’ve got to earn your coin and he’s not really doing that at the moment.’

#1926. Man City lineup vs. RB Leipzig: Predicted XI for Champions League clash

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 18:05, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 18:29

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca will consider making a few changes to his starting lineup for Wednesday’s Champions League clash with RB Leipzig at the Red Bull Arena.

Nearly everyone is fit for the Citizens, with Antoine Semenyo the lone exception as he recovers from a knee injury that requires several weeks of treatment.

Man City were beaten 1-0 by Brighton in the Premier League last weekend, with playmaker Rayan Cherki a notable omission from the starting lineup.

The Frenchman is a strong contender to earn a recall, though, which would likely see either Ayyoub Bouaddi or Enzo Fernandez drop down to the substitutes’ bench.

Should Cherki return in the number 10 role, either Bouddi or Fernandez could link up either Elliot Anderson in a deeper midfield role. Mateo Kovacic, meanwhile, is another central option pushing for a start.

Erling Haaland is all but certain to lead the line; he has scored more goals against Leipzig than any other opponents in his career, netting 12 times in just eight appearances.

Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku may retain their starting spots on the flanks, unless Maresca decides to rotate and recall Allan and Phil Foden, the latter of whom scored a hat-trick in City’s 5-1 UCL win over AEK Athens a fortnight ago.

In defence, Josko Gvardiol may start against his former club but could be replaced at left-back by Nico O'Reilly, while centre-back Marc Guehi will be pushing to replace Abdukodir Khusanov who started alongside captain Ruben Dias last weekend.

Matheus Nunes was fit to play the full 90 minutes against Brighton and could continue at right-back against Leipzig, but Maresca may consider handing either Khusanov or Rico Lewis at start on the right side of a four-man defence.

#1924. Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard says three teams can rival Arsenal for the Premier League title

Steven Gerrard believes Arsenal will retain the Premier League trophy but says three other teams will also ‘pull away’ at the top of the table.

The reigning champions reclaimed their position at the top of the Premier League with a hard-fought 1-0 win over Liverpool on Sunday.

Previous leaders Manchester City suffered another surprising defeat, losing 1-0 at home to Brighton, and Arsenal took full advantage with a narrow win at Anfield thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half goal.

It was another performance from Arsenal that convinced Gerrard that the Premier League trophy will be heading back to the Emirates Stadium after Mikel Arteta ended the club’s 22-year wait last season.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

But Gerrard believes three other clubs – Man City, Liverpool and Chelsea – will also ‘pull away’ from their Premier League rivals and could all challenge Arsenal for the title.

‘Credit to Arsenal because that’s how you win leagues, going to places like Liverpool, being strong, sticking together, and putting in a different type of performance,’ Gerrard told The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Bet.

‘It was full of grit and fight and togetherness, and they got over the line. And they will know that come the end of the season, if they win the league, which I think they will, I haven’t changed my mind from the beginning of the season, they will look back at that more than your four or five-nils where they look fantastic, because I’m sure they will at times.

‘They’ll look at that and think, we went to Anfield, tough crowd to play against, tough Liverpool performance, Andoni Iraola’s got this Liverpool team playing an awful lot better, Liverpool played well and we managed to get out of there with three points.

‘So it could be huge for Arsenal. At this moment in time, nine points behind for Liverpool. So, Liverpool have got work to do if they want to challenge.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But this Arsenal team just look as if they can beat teams in different ways. I think that could be the difference.’

Brighton are third in the Premier League after a memorable win at Manchester City and Gerrard believes Fabian Hurzeler’s side can challenge for a top-four place if not the title.

‘I’m going to put my neck on the line and say that I think they will fall away from that, but that’s not a criticism, because I think they’re a top team with a top manager,’ Gerrard added.

‘I just think to go the distance over the course, I think the stronger teams in the league will pull away a bit, but I certainly think they’re top four contenders and the most dangerous team in the league at the moment to play, because they’re playing without fear.

‘Everyone knows their job in the team, in and out of possession. They’ve improved a lot, I would say, from a defensive point of view. And they’ve got so many dangerous players, people that are comfortable on the ball.

‘They’re fantastic to watch. I think Brighton are more of a threat for the top-four chasers because I think they’re going to push for Champions League places.

‘Over the course, you’re faced with so many different challenges in the Premier League. And I just think where Arsenal’s squad is, and City’s, the Liverpool squad, I just think over the course of the 38 games, the three teams, and Chelsea, when you look at Chelsea in the second half there, I think them teams will pull away a bit over the course.

‘But I think they’re going to push and I think they’re going to go for it and I’m really interested to see how hard they can push. They’re not a title contender, in my opinion.’

#1923. Paul Merson slams Manchester United over Andrey Santos transfer and makes relegation claim

Paul Merson has criticised Manchester United’s decision to sign Andrey Santos and says the Red Devils will be in the relegation zone come December.

Brazilian midfielder Santos has made an inauspicious start to his United career following a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer.

The 22-year-old has started less than half of Manchester United’s games so far this season and struggled to make an impact when he has featured.

Santos is certainly not the only player at Old Trafford under-performing, with Michael Carrick’s side only out of the relegation zone on goal difference following their worst start to the season since the 1980s.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

United’s next five league games are against Aston Villa, Liverpool, Brentford, Newcastle United and Coventry City, and Merson believes they will be sitting in the drop zone by the time they face Frank Lampard’s side in early December.

‘Manchester United play Coventry on the 5th of December and I’d be shocked if they’re not in the bottom three by then,’ Merson told Sky Sports.

‘That’ll be about a third of the season gone then. They might go and get a big result next weekend, Aston Villa looked beatable the other day.

‘I don’t see them getting relegated, absolutely not. But this is not Manchester United and there’s no quick fix, they got it all wrong upstairs.

‘The first window, they went for the forward line but it wasn’t good enough. Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko, they’re nice players but they’re not 20-25 goal-a-season players.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘You’ve got to be a seven, seven and a half out of 10 every week at Manchester United. But they’re a four one week, a nine the next. You can play for Wolves or Brentford and do that, no disrespect.

‘The day you’re a nine you win the match and everyone’s pleased. When you’re a four, people say that’s just the way it is.’

Merson believes a weak and unbalanced midfield is one of Manchester United’s biggest issues, questioning the decision to sign Santos from Chelsea.

‘The midfield they bought – I’d love to see what they saw paying £50m for Andre Santos,’ Merson added. ‘Tell me what you saw that I didn’t when I was watching him every week at Chelsea.

‘Youri Tielemans, he’s a good player but there’s no legs around him in the team. He had legs around him when he was playing at Villa.

‘How do I know there’s no balance in the midfield they’ve bought and they don’t? Two years ago, you’re looking at Casemiro and saying he’s a million miles off it. Now you look at it and think they miss him.

‘And now they say they’ll work on the defence in the next window. It’s madness – you can’t build a house on a puddle. You just can’t. Why not start with the defence first and then go from there?

‘They say they’re going to go and outscore teams but they haven’t bought players who score enough goals.

‘I don’t know where everyone expects them to be. I didn’t expect them to beat Como, I didn’t expect them to beat Bournemouth, I didn’t expect them to beat Chelsea and I don’t expect them to beat Villa.’

Before Manchester United resume their faltering Premier League campaign, they face Italian side Roma in the Champions League.

#1922. Vitor Pereira reveals Nottingham Forest sacking email ‘was not correct’ and sets Premier League title target

By Alexis Pereira | 02 Nov 2026 18:16

Vitor Pereira has revealed that Nottingham Forest sacked him by email at 11.58pm on 30 June, and the Portuguese manager says the way the club went about it ‘was not correct’. Pereira saved Forest from relegation last season, but he has now told The Athletic that he was dismissed with the pre-season already planned.

The 58-year-old was appointed in February, when Forest were three points above the relegation zone, and left them 16th in the Premier League, five points ahead of relegated West Ham United and above Tottenham Hotspur. His contract contained a clause allowing either party to end the agreement before the end of June, and Forest used it with two minutes to spare.

By the time the email arrived, Pereira had reviewed the positives and negatives of the previous season, arranged the pre-season friendlies and even identified possible signings. The players were due to report within weeks, but under a different manager.

‘It was a complete surprise,’ Pereira told The Athletic. ‘I never heard anything that made me feel or think the club no longer counted on me. In the end, they had the right to decide what they wanted for the club, and I accept that.’

He accepted the decision, but not the manner in which owner Evangelos Marinakis’ regime carried it out.

‘The only thing that was not correct was the way they did it - that was the only unfair part. Sending an email... two minutes before midnight, when we had already organised everything for pre-season.’

The late timing had a reason. It came just after Forest learned that Oliver Glasner, who won the Conference League and the 2025 FA Cup with Crystal Palace, was interested in taking over following his exit from Selhurst Park.

‘If they had said to me, “Vitor, although you have organised everything, we have another possibility...”, that would have been fine. That is football,’ Pereira said. ‘In my career, I have spent many years working in different countries, with different cultures. I have plenty of experience, and I know that sometimes football is like that.’

‘But it is fine, I am not the type of person who dwells on the past. I prefer to live in the present, and the present means studying, preparing and getting stronger for the next opportunity. I want to keep the work we did there in my memory. I take with me the affection of the supporters, the people at the club and the players.’

The change has not yet been justified. Forest are second from bottom of the current Premier League table with one win from nine matches, are winless in five and have already been knocked out of the EFL Cup.

Pereira’s job at Forest mirrored his previous Premier League role at Wolverhampton Wanderers, where he took over midway through 2024-25 and secured survival. He stayed on, but was sacked in November last season with Wolves bottom of the table, before they were relegated.

The Portuguese now wants a different path and does not want to take over sides fighting relegation. ‘I am not a firefighter,’ he said.

‘I want to prove my worth by facing and competing with the best managers in the league, and do something special. When you take over a team in the middle of the season, it is because something is not working. That means I have to accept that situation, start with energy and take the right steps to build something solid.’

Pereira says he will look for projects capable of competing for the title and has recently received offers that he might have accepted at another stage of his career.

‘My goal for the future is to compete for titles in the Premier League. If you look at my career before I came to England, you will see that I almost always worked to win titles. I need to take the right steps to reach that level in the Premier League, but that is my goal.’

The last time he took charge of a club among the favourites for domestic honours was Flamengo in 2023, where he failed in the Campeonato Carioca, the Recopa Sudamericana, the Supercopa do Brasil and the Club World Cup, and was sacked within three months.

#1921. Manchester United vs Roma 'set for disruption' amid planned fan protests

Manchester United’s Champions League clash with Roma tonight could be facing disruption.

The Red Devils are looking to snap their nine-game winless run at Old Trafford this evening, but they may have to wait for kick-off with a planned supporters’ protest.

One fan group - the Stretford Enders - has planned to hand out 4,000 green and gold balloons while the Champions League anthem plays around the stadium just before kick-off.

It is thought to be a protest directed at the club’s ownership, the Glazer family and INEOS, with the former overseeing a sharp decline of footballing success in their 21 years of stewardship.

The protests have not been promoted on social media, but reports leaked out in The i and The Athletic ahead of the game.

There was also thought to be plans for a banner to read “No new stadium, we want new owners”, but that will not be shown as UEFA did not sanction it in time for the match, according to The i’s report.

It is believed that a similar protest is planned for this weekend’s Premier League encounter with Aston Villa.

United sit 20th in the Champions League table after two defeats and a victory on their return to Europe’s top table.

That came against minnows Sabah at Old Trafford, before heavy losses at Atletico Madrid and Como.

Further defeats by Bournemouth and Chelsea have thrown manager Michael Carrick’s position into serious question, although the head coach has so far survived the sack, with it being reported that his position will be reassessed during the upcoming November international break.
