#1893. Amorim analyses how Milan were able to overpower Inter: “High pressure and low blocking”

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim refused to be drawn into discussions about the Scudetto, even if he does see improvements from his side.

Milan were in dreamland after 45 minutes of their derby clash against Inter, going in 3-1 up at the break thanks to goals from Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira. As it would turn out, that would be enough to win the bragging rights.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It marked a fourth straight win for Milan in the derby and it reduces the gap to the city rivals back down to four points. While there is still work to be done for the Rossoneri, it feels like a big step forward mentally for the squad.

Amorim spoke to Sky after the full-time whistle to reflect on what was a memorable night for him as a head coach and for the team, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is this the most important victory of the start of the season?

“It’s important. The atmosphere is fantastic, and you can tell after a match like that, especially on a Wednesday like this. It’s clear, even more so after the defeat against Bologna, we wanted to celebrate even more.

“I’m really proud of what my players did, and with so little rest between matches, and especially once again after Bologna, they really fought for the entire match. I’m really proud.”

A nearly perfect team: do you have anything to complain about? You seemed calmer today…

“I try to read and interpret what the team tells me: from the first minute I had the feeling that we were ready to be competitive. The team has always been focused and calm, and so I always had this confidence.”

Is AC Milan a different Milan with Modric, Rabiot, and Pulisic?

“It’s not just those three players, I think it’s the whole atmosphere, the team’s focus. I like the way everyone plays and expresses themselves. For example, I’d like to talk a little about Pavlović and De Vrij.

“They performed well in every game, especially against such a strong team, even in the penalty area. And then, obviously, players like Rabiot, Pulisic, Moreira… they all did very well. All together, I have to say, we were a better team.”

Why Gila on the right and De Winter in the centre?

“Looking at Inter’s stats, we didn’t know if Dimarco would play. They play and cross a lot from the wings and come to create a lot of density in the box, so I think Pavlović and De Winter are the best for crossing.

“That’s the idea: to match our defenders with their attackers, so everyone can play in slightly different defensive roles.”

How did you manage not to concede anything to Inter in the second half?

“I think the lines were closer together; you could see that throughout the match in terms of high pressure and low blocking. The lines were always close together, so the distances were shorter, which obviously also allowed us to run less and stay fresher throughout the game.

“We were very aggressive on the outside, intercepting many crosses before they were launched, which is very difficult against a team like Inter. We defended well by pressing high up, but we also defended well on the sides. We were more aggressive than we usually are.”

“What Cardinale was saying is that the objective is the Scudetto, but it’s important to win these games to make the fans understand that things won’t change in a month, two months, or a year.

“We have to go through this process: you can’t just hire a new coach, replace all the players, and have a new squad for each new coach; that takes time. Then we’ll need magical nights and evenings, and obviously we’ll need to get through difficulties like Wednesday’s and the joy of tonight.

“I want to say that the situation won’t change overnight; it’s not possible. Is the Scudetto possible? I don’t know when, but we still have to be very honest with the fans, and I know that people aren’t stupid; they understand and know the growth this team and this club are in.”

#1892. Peter Schmeichel names Manchester United star who ‘changed the game’ against Roma

Peter Schmeichel praised Manchester United summer signing Youri Tielemans for ‘changing the game’ in the Champions League comeback win over Roma.

United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s looked set to take another blow as Roma stormed into a 2-0 lead at Old Trafford.

Matias Soule took advantage of an alarming amount of room near the United box to put the Italians ahead inside 12 minutes.

Manchester United looked on course for a fourth straight defeat when Donyell Malen doubled Rome’s lead from the penalty spot after Ayden Heaven blocked a shot with his arm.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The home side were booed off at half-time but improved after the break and got a lifeline when Bruno Fernandes scored just before the hour mark from a retaken penalty.

United were still heading for another defeat and Michael Carrick for the sack until Matheus Cunha scored twice late on to complete a memorable European comeback.

Manchester United legend Schmeichel says he felt ‘so sad’ at half-time but believes the game changed upon the introduction of summer signing Tielemans.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The Belgian midfielder replaced the injured Carlos Baleba shortly after half-time and proceeded to ‘change the game’, according to Schmeichel.

‘It’s about time we did something like this,’ Schmeichel told CBS Sports. ‘Manchester United did that type of thing time and time again in the past but it’s been so long.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘At half-time I was so sad about what I had seen in that first 45 minutes because it was bad, it was bad. And then Carlos Baleba goes off injured early in the second half and you’re thinking, this can’t get any worse.

MAN UNITED HAVE TURNED IT AROUND!!! 🔴🔥 From 2-0 down, to 3-2 up at Old Trafford 🤩 pic.twitter.com/ATD8wDlc1e

‘But Youri Tielemans came on and he changed the game. That’s the best I’ve seen him play for Man United and I’m so pleased for him.

‘He came into that midfield and he drove the team forward and he was a leader, it was brilliant to see.

‘That for me can be a big turning point. Those players have now felt what it feels like to be a Manchester United player and play in these big European nights.

‘Coming back from 2-0 down, this is what United have been doing for years. I’m so, so happy for Michael Carrick because he needed this win.’

Schmeichel’s son Kasper, the former Leicester City goalkeeper, also singled out Tielemans for praise after the remarkable comeback at Old Trafford.

‘I said at half-time if you’re going to go down, go down fighting,’ he told BBC Radio 5 Live. ‘You can accept losing if you’ve given absolutely everything and they didn’t do that in the first half.

"This place does magical things, even when it doesn't seem like it's going to happen."Michael Carrick tells @Pschmeichel1 how big that win was at Old Trafford for Manchester United 🔥 pic.twitter.com/7ImYOjMoEl

‘But they did in the second half. The tone was set with Carlos Baleba. It was so unfortunate he got an injury for it but that was a spark.

‘Youri Tielemans came on and that changed the game a little bit. There was a little bit more control.

‘When you’re playing in these games and you’re two down, you’re already done, so you may as well go and give it everything you’ve got. You may as well run around.

‘That should be the standard and now the great thing about it for Michael Carrick is now he has something to refer to.

‘Anytime there’s a difficult situation or pre-match team talk, it’s going to be look what you do when you apply yourselves in that manner then you are impossible to live with.’

The comeback win leaves Manchester United 17th in the Champions League after four games, while Roma slip to 19th.

Carrick’s side return to action on Sunday against Aston Villa while Roma, sitting third in Serie A, play host to Sassuolo.

#1891. Barcelona open talks with Arsenal star Piero Hincapie over January transfer

Barcelona have opened talks with Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie over a January move to the Nou Camp, according to reports in Spain.

Hincapie enjoyed a productive first season at the Emirates Stadium while on loan from Bayer Leverkusen, helping Mikel Arteta’s side win the Premier League and reach the Champions League final.

The Ecuador international made 39 appearances in all competitions, convincing Arsenal bosses to activate their option to make his move permanent for a fee of over £35m.

Hincapie put pen to paper on a five-year contract but his long-term future in north London is already in doubt following a frustrating start to the 2026/27 campaign.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Due to intense competition and some unfortunate injury setbacks, the 24-year-old is still waiting for his first Premier League start and has featured for just 46 minutes in the top-flight.

Hincapie is behind Riccardo Calafiori in Arteta’s pecking order at left-back and saw competition for places in the centre-back positions only increase over the summer with the arrival of England international Ezri Konsa.

Barcelona were linked with a move for Hincapie last summer and the Spanish giants have revived their interest ahead of the January transfer window, according to Spanish outlet SPORT.

The La Liga leaders are keen to sign a new centre-back in January and sporting director Deco has placed Hincapie high up on his list of targets.

It is claimed contact has even been made with Hincapie’s representatives to gauge whether a move would be realistic.

But Arteta is said to be ‘very reluctant’ to lose any first-team players during the winter window given Arsenal expect to be fighting for major trophies once again come the second-half of the season.

Another player of interest to Barcelona is Alessandro Bastoni, the 27-year-old Italy international who has impressed for defending Serie A champions Inter Milan.

Hincapie also attracted interest from Real Madrid last summer, with new Bernabeu boss Jose Mourinho believed to be an admirer of the Ecuador star.

He came on as a late substitute in Arsenal’s hard-fought 1-0 victory over Liverpool on Sunday as the Gunners won at Anfield for the first time in 14 years.

Those three points sent Arsenal to the top of the Premier League, three points above previous leaders Manchester City who have lost their last two games.

Arsenal return to action in the Champions League on Wednesday night, looking to maintain their unbeaten record against Czech giants Slavia Prague.

Arteta’s side won their first two European games without conceding a goal before an entertaining 2-2 draw with German champions Bayern Munich last time out.

#1889. Thierry Henry makes Arsenal comparison in new Manchester United verdict

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Thierry Henry has likened Manchester United’s recent plight to Arsenal’s in the post-Arsene Wenger era.

Before the Red Devils faced Roma in the Champions League, they were coming off a nine-game winless run that saw Michael Carrick mightily close to the sack after a torrid stretch of results that saw United 17th in the Premier League table and 20th in Europe’s premier competition.

They were without a victory since late August, registering just two maximum-point returns all season, against Ipswich Town and minnows Sabah.

Arsenal legend Henry compared United’s current situation to that of his former club when the Gunners were looking to rebuild in Wenger’s final years, through Unai Emery and now Mikel Arteta, who has led the north Londoners to a first top-flight title in 22 years.

“If you go back to the last years of Arsene Wenger, Unai Emery and the beginning of Mikel Arteta, it was a tiny bit toxic,” Henry said on CBS.

“The fans were going amongst each other, asking who the coach should be, who should come and go, having a go at the owners.

“It’s a bit like what’s happening with United now. Surely, along the way, all the coaches they’ve had could have been the answer? Did they give enough time to that one, you don’t know who it could have been? You have guys that are strict, not strict, experienced, not experienced, club legends... it didn’t work.

“You’re telling me that none of those coaches could have turned it around? Were they given time to turn it around? Arteta at times didn’t have great runs in the league; didn’t finish where Arsenal are supposed to finish. They kept him.

“Now everyone is saying he’s a great coach. If he didn’t have the time to show that he was a good coach, we would have said that he was inexperienced, couldn’t handle it and couldn’t win.”

Carrick oversaw a 3-2 win against Roma on Tuesday in a dramatic comeback at Old Trafford that had threatened to turn toxic once more as United fell 2-0 down inside 18 minutes against the in-form Italians.

They roared back in the second period to claim all three points, in a result that will give their under-fire boss more time as they prepare to face Aston Villa at home this weekend.

#1888. Barcelona, Lille and Brighton and Hove Albion scout Estoril teenager Jordan Arnolin

By Alexis Pereira | 02 Nov 2026 19:19, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 19:19

Barcelona are reportedly taking a close interest in Jordan Arnolin, but the Estoril centre-back is also attracting attention in France and the Premier League.

Barcelona are not only looking to sign established players to strengthen their defence. The Catalan club, leader in LaLiga, are also scouting young European talents, and according to Portuguese newspaper Record, they sent a representative to the Estadio do Dragao on Saturday to watch 18-year-old Arnolin.

The interest comes as Barcelona have spent several months trying to strengthen their back line. The sporting department is working on several profiles, with the aim of finding a centre-back who can give Hansi Flick more guarantees.

The name of Inter Milan stalwart Alessandro Bastoni has been mentioned insistently in recent months, most recently by Sky Sports. The Italy international would be an especially expensive operation, however, and Inter have no reason to make his departure easy. Against that backdrop, a young player with high potential is another route for the Barcelona hierarchy, and Arnolin fits that logic.

Barcelona will have to contend with two other suitors. According to Record, Lille and Brighton and Hove Albion also sent representatives to the Dragao to monitor the young Portuguese.

For Lille, the move would fit a well-established recruitment policy of backing high-potential players who can take a step up and increase in value. The northern French club have regularly used that model to bring in players who are not yet well known to the wider public. Brighton are a far stronger financial rival, with greater resources than Lille and their own reputation for finding talent. Their ability to attract young players and offer them exposure in the Premier League is another argument in their favour.

Lille face a stiff challenge. Barcelona have a sporting and media pull that is unmatched, and even though Arnolin would probably not walk straight into Flick’s starting line-up, joining the Catalan club would be hard for an 18-year-old to turn down.

Lille do have one strong argument in playing time. With heavy competition in the Barcelona squad, particularly at centre-back, the young Portuguese could have to wait for first-team chances, while a gradual path to the Lille first team looks easier to envisage.

The financial side remains a factor, too. Brighton have more room for manoeuvre, and Barcelona keep considerable economic strength and international appeal, despite their well-known budget constraints. Lille will probably have to rely on their sporting project and their ability to support the defender’s progress.

Another element could complicate negotiations. Arnolin has just signed his first professional contract with Estoril, running until June 2029, so the club are under no pressure to sell. Lille have a card to play, but they will need to be convincing to beat two very serious competitors.

#1887. Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

“I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

“We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”

What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

“We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola said. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”

Why they didn’t follow the plan that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

Those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

“We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”

Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

A really soft one, if you give that, they’ll be more in the future, I’m not a fan of that.

Their heads are a little down but we know we had many challenges, we’re in a huge transition phase at the moment.

It’s a brave project but I like the challenge, working with young lads, they were tired. Lewis Miley just came back from an injury but they did an amazing job and it’s just about getting adapted to the league.

The crowd here is unbelievable and the quality. Every change can be decisive and it’s something I really enjoy. We’re clear in our approach and you can adjust in the game if you plan ahead.

It’s not the result you want, but scoring in the last minute gives us a better feeling. I value that the players never gave up. I’m sure we had more chances, it’s unfair they’re winning very early and overall, I think we’ve had the better chances.

We were probably in the first half not finishing anything, we had a lot of balls on the edge but we needed to shoot. We don’t finish play and then they win on the counter-attack.

The players coming from the bench gave us energy and you can feel the way we want to play.

Overall, we played a lot in their half and had good moments and phases on the ball. The first goal was more difficult to defend, Anthony Elanga is a fast player. The second, I think we had the numbers but sometimes you have to finish the play and try and win the ball.

What a special club, what a special man, that’s why we gave him a big credit. The fans were unbelievable today. I think we gave them so much back today and that’s what we need to give them all season.

We know we needed to give the fans something after this period so that’s why we tried to start fast. The fans pushed us until the end.

It was my best [performance for Newcastle] so far. New manager, new role. I’m so pleased to be here. I hope today I showed I’m really happy.

It’s rough, especially 30 seconds before the end of the game, but that’s a huge step for us. That’s the mentality we need to have through the season. The manager came three weeks ago and gave us a lot of information. Now we show on the pitch we are ready for the season. We needed this win to make a statement but in the end we draw. We have so much to work on.

To be honest, I didn’t even hear the referee’s whistle. I had to look at him if I can go. I was practising a lot during the pre-season. We didn’t have any penalties during games, but in training. We need to take the positivity of the first game and move on.

More than 50,000 fans in the stadium against you. You can’t hear your own voice. That’s why I love football and that’s why I am doing it.

To come here is always tough. Everybody knows the [Newcastle] fans are unbelievable. They have a great team and a manager - new but he has proven himself in many other clubs. But we were prepared and we needed to be closer to each other under a new manager as well. We needed to know what was going on in the game. It’s a good thing coming back into the game after 2-1 down.

If I am honest, we should have won. But that’s football. You don’t win easy in the Premier League - doesn’t matter who you play against. We have to be aware of that and we need to take care in the next game.

🗣️ "It's knee on knee, it's a foul"Micah Richards and Daniel Sturridge analyse Lewis Hall's foul which led to Liverpool's late penalty. pic.twitter.com/NRw406sTcZ

14 - Liverpool remain unbeaten on MD1 in the Premier League in each of the last 14 seasons (since 2013-14), the longest active run in the competition.Spirited. pic.twitter.com/3rluUnSBhu

I think they did the right thing, easy to say now of course, by not giving Isak the penalty. There is enough pressure on in the 96th minute without all that would have entailed. Nor was Isak having the best of games.

A familiar feeling after last season. Newcastle concede a last kick of the game penalty. Should have held on for the win. It was a soft penalty, Hall dangled out a knee rather than a leg and Munoz made sure he ran into it. But as soon as it's given on the field never going to be…

The points are shared, and Lewis Hall has his hands on his knees. Jaissle protests with the officials. This was a stirring home performance from Newcastle which should build confidence for the season ahead. An irrepressible showing from Wissa was the biggest positive. Iraola will be pleased to get back on the coach with a draw after what was quite a ragged Liverpool performance, their midfield balance looked off.

What a magnificent penalty from Szoboszlai, Hornicek had no chance, and Liverpool have surely snatched a point.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

What theatre that would be... Gakpo has the ball in his hands. But no, it’s going to be Szoboszlai.

With the last kick of the game, practically. Kerkez launched the ball forward, Van Dijk competed for a header, Munoz pounced on the seconds, and his pace carried enough threat to prompt Hall to step across the winger and make contact with his knee.

#NEWLIV – 90+6' The referee's call of penalty for the challenge by Hall on Muñoz was checked and confirmed by VAR. REF: "He doesn't play the ball. He makes clear contact". VAR: "It's knee into thigh contact. Confirming the on-field decision of penalty".

So, so poor from Frimpong who hesitates to put a cross in, takes a couple of unconvincing touches, and then commits a foul. Mac Allister. Wissa receives a standing ovation, replaced by Schar.

Gakpo runs down a blind alley, and it is another blunt Liverpool attack. Time running out for them now.

Liverpool corner, won by Lewis Koumas who lacked support but his cross deflects behind.

Hornicek palms away Szoboszlai’s delivery. This has been strong Premier League debut from the goalkeeper.

Newcastle have a throw deep in Liverpool territory after more good work from Wissa, and chaotic defending from Liverpool. Atwell has booked Gakpo for an earlier foul on Wissa.

There will be FIVE minutes of added time.

Murphy with another wonderful cross through the Liverpool six-yard box, but no player in black and white was gambling for a tap in. Liverpool just about still in with a sniff.

Cheers at St James’ Park as Thiaw ushers the ball behind as Kerkez tried to get in behind. Then Frimpong’s touch lets him down, not for the first time.

An aimless cross from Liverpool, and Munoz is penalised at the back post for a push. Liverpool have lacked clarity and intelligence in the last third today, but there is still time.

Big save by Alisson! He narrows the angle to deny Wissa the goal his performance deserves. How important could that prove to be? Liverpool have the ball again.

Liverpool with a long spell of possession in the final third, trying to tire Newcastle legs, but Frimpong’s cross is a little too high for Isak to generate any power with the header. Newcastle are just starting to sit in a touch.

Munoz runs down a blind alley, more sound defending from Lewis Hall and the Newcastle players can see the finish line now. They will be only too aware of how they lost this game in the last minute 12 months ago, though.

Szoboszlai shoots against the well, and the Araujo is booked for bundling over a Newcastle defender. Wissa thought he was away for Newcastle but the flag goes up for offside.

Frimpong does well to keep things alive for Liverpool, and there are half-hearted appeals for a handball penalty but Thiaw was down by his side. Another Liverpool sub: Lewis Koumas is on for Gravenberch.

The long throw is headed away, but Murphy catches Mac Allister and Liverpool have a free-kick in a crossing position. Though you never can tell with Szoboszlai around.

Here come those changes from Newcastle: Murphy and Bamba on for Elanga and Miley. Hall’s delivery from the free-kick won by Wissa was poor.

Liverpool have Newcastle penned in, but Munoz’s pass is overhit and Newcastle have a goal kick. Jaissle is about to introduce Jacob Murphy from the bench. Wissa, Newcastle’s best player by a stretch, does well to win a free-kick high up the pitch from Szoboszlai.

Araujo is on for Jacquet at the back for Liverpool, who have just threatened again. Szoboszlai hacked down but the referee waved play on, and Kerkez could not get enough curl on his cross or else Isak would have had a free header.

Willock lifts in a teasing cross from the right, Alisson palms the ball back into danger, and Ramsey cracks a shot wide of the post. Hard to say whether this game is going 3-1 or 2-2 but the scoring is surely not over.

Was that Isak’s moment? Gakpo rolls the ball back to Isak in a good shooting position just inside the box, but he slices his left-footed effort well over the bar. More cheers from the Newcastle fans.

Newcastle really should have three! Defence-splitting pass from Miley to release Hall, who feeds a teasing cross into the six-yard box, but Wissa could only get studs on it. Better connection and that was a goal. Liverpool so fragile at the back, though.

Stuart Atwell has been guessing on decisions throughout this game, and Jacob Ramsey has just been booked for what looked a clean challenge on Isak, who produced a lovely turn initially. Newcastle survive the free-kick.

But then Gakpo has acres of space to run into, but Botman saves the day in the box. The game is haywire at the moment.

Here come the Liverpool changes: Ngumoha, who was the match-winner last season here, Wirtz are the players off, replaced by Munoz and Mac Allister.

Liverpool will be kicking themselves, they had Newcastle on the ropes. Iraola is preparing a triple sub. Willock was the goalscorer, but it was also a brilliant assist from Wissa.

The equaliser had been coming but that was really poor from a defensive perspective as everyone backed off Cody Gakpo and let him pick his spot.

You also have to question the decision to keep Will Osula on. He was obviously struggling to move freely and it has meant Newcastle did not have an out ball.

But, just as I was going to be critical of manager Matthias Jassile one of his substitutes puts Newcastle back in front and it a brilliant goal. Magnificent build up play from Wissa, who skipped away from three Liverpool players, but it is even better from Joe Willock who takes the pass in his stride, shows great skill t o take it on jis stride and away from Frimpong and the finish is sublime, curled into the bottom corner.

Jaissle can claim that as a magical substitution, but it is superb individual goal from Joe Willock. Another Newcastle counter-attack, Wissa does brilliantly to wriggle away from three players in midfield, and Willock dribbles inside Frimpong before arcing a shot into the far corner. Outstanding finish.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

Jaissle with a double sub immediately after conceding: Joe Willock and Jacob Ramsey are on, replacing William Osula and Sean Steur who was a little slack on the Gakpo goal.

The game is one-way traffic, Liverpool looking to turn the screw.

The man linked with a move to Spurs all summer has equalised for Liverpool. He had a sighter a few minutes earlier, and it was too easy for Gakpo to receive the ball behind Newcastle’s midfield, and he had time to pick out the far corner with a clean hit from outside the box. Game on.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

Just two touches inside the Newcastle penalty area from Isak so far, he has been subdued. Nice idea from Gakpo, chopping inside from the left, and curling a shot not far wide of the top corner.

Good defending from Lewis Hall up against Ngumoha, before Van Dijk passes the ball straight of play. Wissa wanted a free-kick for a challenge from behind by Gravenberch but the referee judged he touched the ball first.

Scramble at the back post from the Liverpool corner, but then a loose touch from Wirtz prompts a Newcastle break and there was a chance for Elanga to dribble into the box but he put the breaks on.

The game is already really stretched, holes appearing in Liverpool’s midfield. Wissa’s poked through ball towards Osula was just a tad overhit.

Liverpool have made a sharp start from kick off, winning a corner.

Just because it is a manager’s first game, we shouldn’t pull our punches. That was a scandalous first half performance from Liverpool and there is absolutely no difference in watching them now compared to what they offered through much of last season. Maybe the disappointment wasn’t about the man in the dugout. Maybe it was about the players wearing the Red shirt.

5 & 18 - 5 - Liverpool have conceded in the opening five minutes on MD1 of a Premier League season for the very first time.The Reds are winless in 18 Premier League away games when falling 1-0 behind (D6 L12) since beating Crystal Palace 2-1 in December 2023.Baptism. pic.twitter.com/K1HF2wNRVP

Newcastle will be delighted to go in leading the game at half time but there were some worrying signs before the break.

They had stopped getting up the pitch and were invited a lot of pressure from Liverpool. Will Osula has clearly picked up an injury – he took a whack on his achilles midway through the half – and will surely need to be replaced by Nick Woltemade in the second half with Yoane Wissa moving up top.

Alexander Isak has been on the receiving end of a number of heavy tackles and has looked pretty miserable so far on his return to St James’ Park.

But Liverpool are not going to keep getting into dangerous positions and fail to capitalise on them. Things for Matthias Jaissle to sort out before the second half.

LFC Midfield all bombing forward happened all pre season, madness!

Plenty of possession for Liverpool, but not enough cutting edge of crispness in their play in the final third. On top of that problem, they were vulnerable to Newcastle’s pace and direct play early on although that threat abated as the half progressed. Jaissle will be delighted with the commitment and application of his players, but Osula may have to come off with a knock.

Isak hooks a pass towards Frimpong straight out of play, causing much mirth among the home fans.

Foul given against Wissa on Gravenberch, and the Newcastle forward needs to be careful on a yellow. I’m not sure there was any contact at all. Wissa drags a shot across the face of Liverpool’s goal and wide.

Gravenberch with a speculative shot which is blocked, before Dedic blasts the ball off Gakpo to win a goal kick. Dan Burn is watching on from the stands, Newcastle’s new club captain who is absent because of a rolled ankle. Also up there in the gods is England manager Thomas Tuchel.

Much better cross from Frimpong, but Dedic clears at the back post for a Liverpool corner. Danger as Gakpo flicks the ball on at the neat post, and the ball bounces off Botman and behind for another corner. Gravenberch tries a cute reverse pass towards Isak, but it deflects through to Hornicek. Isak has been ever so quiet.

William Osula is hobbling up top for Newcastle, which is a worry because has been a menace so far. The same can be said of Yoane Wissa who is having a stormer as a second striker, dropping into midfield at times.

Stuart Atwell being a little card happy, now Lewis Miley is shown a yellow for a foul on Gravenberch. Just looked a regulation midfield foul, not sure a booking was necessary.

Osula took the free-kick, straight into the wall, but his follow up effort deflects off Szoboszlai and behind for a corner. Excellent delivery from Lewis Hall, cleared by Van Dijk.

Wirtz and Isak do well down the left to start a Liverpool counter with runners forward, but Frimpong’s delivery from the right is atrocious.

Liverpool starting to monopolise possession, without a crafty final pass. Kerkez has been booked for holding Elanga, who is giving him a going over on Newcastle’s right flank.

Then Barnes rolls inside Frimpong and drives inside, and the Liverpool right-back is booked for a challenge from behind. May well have been a harsh call, both plays were grasping for a piece of shirt.

Both of Liverpool’s full-backs on yellows now.

Wissa booked for a mistimed challenge, and Liverpool have a free-kick 30 yards out. Szoboszlai is thinking about a shot... but he blasts his shot straight into the wall.

Osula then does very well to make it stick and drag Newcastle up the pitch but the move fizzles out.

It’s an experience in itself watching Andoni Iraola on the sideline. He’s going to have clocked up 10,000 steps for sure by the final whistle and his increasing animation is indicative of Liverpool’s anaemic start. You would expect Liverpool to score at some point but this is a team that has lots of questions to answer.

Isak down on the turf after a strong challenge by Lewis Hall, no foul given much to the delight of the Newcastle fans.

Then the home team cut through Liverpool again, Wissa with a glorious outside of the foot pass behind Jacquet for the run of Osula, but the Liverpool defender just about got a toe to the ball as the striker closed in on Alisson. Great challenge in the end from the wrong side.

Nice counter-movement between Elanga and Dedic the right-back. Elanga faked to drop inside, taking Kerkez and Gakpo with him, and Miley’s switch found Dedic on the outside. Cross is blocked, and Newcastle have a corner. Cleared, and then a poor Szoboszlai pass is blocked when there was a chance to release Wirtz on the counter.

It feels like all the 50:50s are dropping Newcastle’s way at the moment. It has been a very energetic start, the question is whether that is sustainable across the game so early in the season. The tempo will surely drop at some point.

Peter Beardsley, Tino Asprilla and Shaka Hislop among Keegan’s former players watching on.

Hornicek with his first big save of the game, tipping Wirtz’s shot around the post. Newcastle failed to deal with a Kerkez cross and the ball dropped to the German for a snap shot. Newcastle defend the corner.

“There’s only one greedy b-----d,” is the chant from the Newcastle fans (aimed at Isak, for the uninitiated).

Wissa goes down looking for a foul but nothing doing, but there are cheers from the home fans as Isak is beaten to a header and then Sean Steur turns away from pressure well in midfield. There is more bite about the home team in the challenges than Liverpool, Jaissle will be delighted with this.

Echoes of last season with Liverpool’s defence looking suspect against direct play, Alisson with an unconvincing intervention outside his penalty area after the ball held up. He is fortunate that Wissa did not connect with the volley when there was a chance to lob the goalkeeper.

What a difference a year makes. Anthony Elanga was played in on goal against Aston Villa on his Premier League debut for Newcastle United 12 months ago. He looked nervous and hit a tame effort too close to the goalkeeper.

It is fair to say that was a sign of things to come for the winger who endured a miserable first season on Tyneside following a high-profile £55m move from Nottingham Forest. He looked drained of confidence and lacked the composure and technical ability to succeed in black and white stripes.

Fast forward 12 months and he has just taken a very similar chance against Liverpool. The speed of Will Osula sent the visiting defence into retreat, and his pace and excellent first touch set up the chance, which he finished clinically.

That was the player Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer. It was the player Newcastle supporters thought was going to offer a major upgrade in the right wing position.

If Elanga has a better season this time around it will be a huge boost to new manager Matthias Jaissle.

Elanga vs Kerkez is a match-up which looks advantageous for Newcastle, the Liverpool left-back is at full tilt to get back and by a foul after a lofted Wissa pass over his head towards the rapid Sweden winger.

This is a very open game already, and Liverpool are back on the front foot. Szoboszlai whips in a free-kick which appears to glance of Van Dijk’s head, but the referee awards a corner. Hall clears, but Newcastle do not clear their lines and Gakpo’s shot is blocked by Thiaw.

Liverpool caught out on the break, but it is a really well-executed goal from Newcastle’s perspective. Gravenberch should have let fly at the other end, but after the move broke down Osula was able to receive in space and turn to face Van Dijk and Jacquet. He waited for the support of Elanga to arrive, and he burned down the outside of Kerkez. Well-weighted pass put him through, and the finish across Alisson was ideal.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

Lewis Hall wins a challenge at the edge of the box which receives a roar of approval from the crowd, but Liverpool quickly settle into a long spell of possession, with Gravenberch turning away from pressure, but neglecting to shoot.

This already has the feel of a very helter-skelter game. Newcastle won a free-kick inside 20 seconds, clipped into the penalty area but it was claimed by Alisson. Then a Liverpool attack swept from one end to the other with Wirtz’s shot blocked at the edge of the box. This should be tasty.

That roar turns to vociferous boos as Alexander Isak takes the kick-off.

They would have still been clapping until tomorrow if the whistle hadn’t been blown by referee Stuart Attwell to start the game but the flip from adulation for Kevin Keegan to absolute vitriol towards Alexander Isak was incredible. 50,000 in black and white are singing a song aimed at him. The only two words we can get away with printing are “ole, ole!” - use your imagination for what might have preceded it!

A period of applause for Kevin Keegan at St James' Park 👏❤️ pic.twitter.com/AsSGOkpVPN

There is a minute’s applause for Keegan, which ends with a defending roar.

Liverpool have just taken to the field for their warm up, predictably to a back drop of pantomime booing. But there is a nice touch from the club, as each member of Andoni Iraola’s squad is wearing a jersey with “Keegan 7” on the back. It’s going to be a day of heavy emotion.

Alan Shearer was one of those fans holding up a white card:

The Keegan quote on the Newcastle banner is: “I want people to dream about their football club. They should, we should all be dreamers at heart. Some people are the opposite and say ‘we can’t do that’, but when you ask them why, they can’t give a reason. Well, I say, ‘Why not?’”

Banners are being unfurled in the Gallowgate End. Alan Shearer and Stuart Pearce are in the stands, and Les Ferdinand is pitchside speaking on Sky.

As you know it’s a transition phase and a huge challenge. There will be some activity in the transfer market new week, hopefully, but we go for it, we are as ready as we can be. That’s something we want to show the fans, we want to go all in.

As soon as I saw him on the pitch, I was falling in love. He is a great guy with great potential.

I’m not worried. As a manager, a player or a squad, if it is against you you want to play this kind of games.

Difficult call, Jeremy has very good skills with the ball, without the ball they will be very demanding today, playing against Wissa and Osula.

Alexander Isak is going to be in for the sort of hostile afternoon unseen in English football for years.

Not since Michael Owen has a player left Newcastle and been so universally despised. Owen was accused of ducking out of a relegation battle to ensure he secured a lucrative free transfer move after an injury-ravaged spell in the North East.

If anything, Isak was even worse, He went on strike, refusing to play for the club again, despite having three years left on his contract, in order to force a move to Liverpool. It felt like the ultimate betrayal and crossed a line with Geordies. They will love you and worship players as good as Isak, but if you behave like the Sweden international did you become the ultimate villain.

Isak was a superb player in black and white stripes, arguably their best since the takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund in 2021. He was top goalscorer two years running and was the focal point of Eddie Hower’s attack as they qualified for the Champions League twice and won the Carabao Cup.

He could have been a Geordie legend, but he left in such an ugly and acrimonious fashion. Isak forced Newcastle to buckle from their not for sale stance, rejecting a pay rise and a new contract, insisting he would never play for the club again even if they refused to sell him, that he will be tarnished forever.

It is sad in many ways and shows the ugly side of the game. I’m told he does regret the manner of his exit, especially his falling out with Howe. They have not spoken since. It has weighed heavily on him since his move to Anfield.

Looks like Rio Ngumoha will play on the right flank with Cody Gakpo left, Wirtz in the No 10 role behind Isak.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Frimpong, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Gravenberch, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak

The Reds to take on Newcastle in our season opener ✊ #NEWLIV

Barnes, Wissa, Osula and Elanga start in what could be a front four. Lewis Miley and Sean Steur, just 20 and 18 respectively, will need to get through an immense amount of work in midfield.

Newcastle United XI: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Miley, Steur; Elanga, Wissa, Barnes; Osula

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Bobby Moncur are the representatives of both clubs with wreaths, and Shola Ameobi is behind Dalglish. Ian Rush is also in attendance, who spent one season on Tyneside in the twilight of his career when Dalglish was the manager.

There will be a powerful expression of unity between Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters in memory of their shared icon, Kevin Keegan, before this afternoon’s game.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

The sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan means that for the first time since Liverpool came into existence in 1892, the prospect of them going through the season without fielding a player who was born in the city for a game is real. That will surely sting Liverpool fans more than most, given the city’s strong sense of regional identity. You can read more on the subject in this article by Dominic King. Trent on loan in January, anyone?

He has also not sugar-coated anything. Jaissle knows he is up against it. Time is the enemy, given how late he arrived in pre-season and he understands the size of the task ahead.

These are early days, but the energy and purpose he has brought to the job have impressed everyone at all levels of the club. Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.Full team news on the way shortly.

#1884. Ezri Konsa, the best Arsenal signing of last window, gives Mikel Arteta a welcome selection headache

By Alexis Pereira | 02 Nov 2026 19:29

Arsenal’s outstanding defensive display in the 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday ended a 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at their rival’s ground. The result was built on superb organisation and discipline in front of David Raya’s goal, and one of the standout names was Ezri Konsa.

The England defender produced a top-level performance to secure the clean sheet. According to Opta, he won eight of nine duels, made eight clearances, five tackles, five recoveries and two blocks, and won two fouls.

For the first time in the Premier League era, Liverpool did not register a single shot on target in a game at Anfield, a mark that highlights the outstanding collective defending and the performance of the centre-back pairing. Konsa’s understanding with Gabriel Magalhaes makes it look as though the two have played together for many seasons.

So far, Konsa has maintained the high level he showed at his former club, Aston Villa. He has made only 13 appearances for the Gunners this season, yet he already merits the label of a successful signing. His assured displays have almost made supporters forget who held the position before his arrival.

The 29-year-old joined Arsenal in August for £51m to replace William Saliba, who suffered a serious back injury that forced him off in the World Cup semi-final between France and Spain.

Saliba, who is not expected to return until the end of this month, had been one of Arsenal’s defensive foundations in recent seasons, and the club decided to bring in an outside name, even though Christian Mosquera, Piero Hincapie, Riccardo Calafiori and Jurrien Timber could all have played there.

From here, boss Mikel Arteta will have the kind of selection headache every manager dreams of. Konsa and Saliba will compete at a high level to play alongside Gabriel Magalhaes, and Arsenal can only benefit.

The season is long and the Gunners will compete for every trophy. Having elite players both on the pitch and on the bench is essential to withstand the physical strain over the months ahead.

In recent seasons, Arsenal have made good signings, especially in defence, such as Timber, Calafiori and Hincapie. Konsa shares a key characteristic with those names. His versatility, as he can also play at right-back, gives Arteta a range of options very few European clubs can match, and over a long season that could prove decisive.

#1882. Bruno Fernandes sends Michael Carrick sack message after dramatic Manchester United victory

Bruno Fernandes has insisted that no-one’s job needed saving after Manchester United secured a dramatic 3-2 victory over Roma.

The Red Devils went into the Champions League clash off the back of a nine-match winless run that saw pressure pile on manager Michael Carrick, with most expecting him to be relieved of his duties following the 3-0 demolition by Bournemouth, which followed the 4-1 thrashing at Como.

He ultimately survived the sack and stayed on for another defeat, this time at Chelsea, and questions were being asked once more as United fell 2-0 down to the in-form Italian side inside 18 minutes at Old Trafford.

Matias Soule and Donyell Malen got the goals in an awful first half for the hosts, which was darkened by supporters throwing gold and green balloons and tennis balls from the stands onto the pitch in protest at the club’s plight, while colourful chanting was directed at the directors’ box, where Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada sat watching on.

Captain Fernandes, who was dropped by Carrick against Bournemouth for criticism he made about the manager’s approach in the Como defeat, missed a penalty and cut a frustrated figure at times on Tuesday, but luck smiled down on the Portuguese as he was able to reprieve himself from the spot after an encroachment allowed him to retake his 12-yard kick.

Afterwards, the No8 insisted that Carrick’s job was not in question in his first interview since his Como comments.

"No, we don't need to save anyone's job,” Fernandes said.

"The club needed that win, the players needed that win. It's something that we needed as a group of players together with the staff.

"We've been working so hard to get out of this situation altogether. It's been tough, there's been a lot of speculation in the media, a lot of lies around many things that have happened in this club. Between me and the manager, that we had cleared the air, then after, nothing of that happened.

"The manager took a decision of putting myself on the bench because I wasn't performing at that level. Everyone felt that it was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right.

"The manager is the one that makes the decisions. I have to accept them, I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, in the staff and every player that is in this club.

"It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me.

Tenerife centre-forward De Miguel sustained severe head and chest injuries following a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono, who was subsequently shown a red card for the challenge.

Owono had raced out of his his goal in an attempt to clear the ball when the deadly coming together occurred in the closing stages of Monday’s Spanish second-division contest.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the hours that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Meanwhile, the Spanish FA postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches that were scheduled to take place on Tuesday to allow for time to ‘grieve over this sad loss’.

Owono is yet to make a public statement in relation to the incident and Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, has said the 25-year-old was ‘experiencing profound distress and anguish’ following the news of De Miguel’s death.

‘There are moments when football stops making sense. Moments that stay with you forever and make you realise just how fragile life can be. ‘Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy that we could never have imagined experiencing on a football pitch.

‘I would also like to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who has been deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know what kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

‘We know that no words can ease such pain, but we want them to know that we stand by their side and deeply share their sadness.

‘We also want to extend all our support to CD Tenerife, its players, its technical staff, its workers, and its fans. From the very first moment, we have been in contact with them and are at their disposal for anything they may need.

‘Likewise, we are in contact with LaLiga, the Government of Andorra, and the relevant organizations to offer all our collaboration and the necessary support during these very difficult times. We have also requested the postponement of the next match against RCD Mallorca, as we believe these are moments of profound grief in which respect and support for all those affected must prevail.

‘What has happened has had a great emotional impact on our players, the technical staff, and everyone who is part of FC Andorra. These are especially tough times for everyone, and we want to ensure that no one has to face them alone. For this reason, the club is providing psychological support to all those who need it.

‘We are a team, on and off the field. Now more than ever, we must stand together, support each other, and take care of one another.

‘All of football and all of sports are in mourning. These are moments of profound sadness in which we must remain united, support those who need it most, and show the utmost respect.

‘Our most sincere condolences to Jesús’s family and to everyone at CD Tenerife. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

#1880. Michael Carrick spotted ordering Man Utd star to leave the pitch after Roma win

Michael Carrick was spotted telling Matheus Cunha to leave the pitch immediately after the final whistle in Manchester United’s comeback victory over AS Roma.

The Brazil international scored twice as United fought back from two goals behind to win 3-2 at Old Trafford on Tuesday night. After Bruno Fernandes’ penalty, Cunha pounced on a defensive error to level the contest before firing home a winner on 86 minutes.

The former Wolves star removed his shirt and leapt into the crowd in celebration, earning himself a booking. A second yellow followed in injury time for an overzealous challenge as United held on.

Cunha slowly trudged around the perimeter of the pitch as he made his way to the tunnel, desperate to see the final minutes of the match play out.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

He briefly disappeared down the tunnel before reemerging to join the post-match celebrations after the final whistle had blown.

But TV cameras picked up Carrick appearing to tell his player to go straight to the dressing room with Cunha seen pleading with his boss on the pitch. The unhappy Brazilian eventually made his way back down the tunnel, flanked by a club official.

IFAB rules, which also govern Champions League matches, state that a player who has been sent off ‘must leave the vicinity of the field of play and the technical area’ and cannot return, even after the full-time whistle has been blown.

Cunha is set to miss United’s next Champions League match away to Sporting CP on 25 November.

Victory handed Carrick a lifeline with United’s focus now shifting to Aston Villa on Sunday.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘At half-time, I was wanting them to be more positive, if anything, and not get too disappointed and frustrated,’ said Carrick.

‘When you keep trying to do something, the easiest thing is feeling sorry for yourself. If something goes wrong, you get disappointed. That’s not going to help anybody. We might as well all go home if that’s the case. We’ve got to keep looking for the next moment, the next solution.

‘I don’t like to keep talking to the lads about what this place can do and the history and what’s gone before too much, but it’s there.

‘This place does magical things, it’s done it before and it’ll do it over and over again at some point in the future. There’s just something in this place that when we do have these types of nights, we do it the hard way.

‘But one moment can flip the whole place in a different direction. I spoke about that with the boys. Let’s have one moment that can trigger it. And we had that.’

#1879. Barcelona's Gavi stance 'revealed' amid transfer speculation surrounding 22-year-old

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 19:49

Barcelona are reportedly unwilling to discuss an exit for Gavi, with the club viewing the midfielder as a vital player despite his struggles for action this term.

The 22-year-old has been restricted to just 191 minutes of football across seven appearances for Barcelona at the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

The Spaniard has only started twice in La Liga this term, while his three appearances in the Champions League have come off the bench.

There is currently a host of speculation surrounding Gavi's future, with some reports claiming that the midfielder could be allowed to leave Camp Nou for the right price.

However, according to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, Barcelona have no desire to allow Gavi to leave, viewing the Spaniard as an important part of their plans moving forward.

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick was asked about Gavi during his press conference on Monday, with the team preparing to face Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday.

“We all know his quality and Gavi is always an option, but once the match starts that option might disappear and you can’t always stick to your initial plan. I’ve spoken to him and the important thing is that he has confidence," Flick told reporters.

Gavi has been with Barcelona since the age of 11, progressing to the first team in 2021, and he has represented the Catalan outfit on 173 occasions, scoring 10 goals and registering 18 assists for the club in all competitions.

Worryingly, Gavi has already had two severe knee injuries in the early stages of his career, first being absent between November 2023 and September 2024.

Gavi was also missing between August 2025 and March 2026, and fitness problems have made it difficult for him to find consistency in recent seasons.

It is understood that a number of major clubs are keeping a close eye on the situation in the event that Barcelona signal a willingness to let him depart.

Barcelona will follow Tuesday's clash against Villa with a La Liga fixture away to Atletico Madrid ahead of the November international break.

#1878. Michael Carrick issues Manchester United injury latest after Carlos Baleba blow

Michael Carrick will be sweating over the fitness of Carlos Baleba after the Manchester United midfielder hobbled off on Tuesday.

The Cameroon international was forced off with a hamstring injury in the 3-2 victory over Roma at Old Trafford, as the Red Devils roared back from 2-0 down to secure a much-needed victory.

It is a result that eases the pressure on their under-fire manager, who had overseen a nine-match winless run which had seen his job brought into question.

He was spared the sack after heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth a fortnight ago, taking charge last weekend at Chelsea, where they also lost 2-0.

His players rallied for him in the second half in the Champions League, however, after a dismal first-half showing that saw their visitors go 2-0 up thanks to Matias Soule and Donyell Malen’s quick-fire strikes.

Baleba was a bright spark for the home side in an otherwise absymal display, with the summer recruit showing bursts of energy from midfield, looking to support attacking moves.

An early power into the Roma box in the second period was what did the damage, however, as he pulled up grasping his hamstring in agony inside the first minute of the second half.

It comes as a fresh blow to the former Brighton midfielder, who arrived in the north west in the summer with a pre-existing ankle problem that scuppered his start to life in his new colours.

Carrick issued an update on Baleba afterwards, and he will be praying that his new signing will only be out for a short time.

"I haven't got any more news on Carlos at this stage, but obviously it looks like it’s his hamstring," the United head coach said.

"So we'll just have to assess what that looks like. I mean, initially, it doesn't look great. Timelines? I haven't got much more to give you."

United face Aston Villa at Old Trafford this weekend before the November international break.

#1877. “It’s not a surprise to me” – Pulisic delighted with Milan’s performance in derby win

Christian Pulisic believes AC Milan recorded an important win against Inter in the derby, but they must keep their heads down and continue working.

Milan claimed the bragging rights in the derby, winning 3-1 at San Siro tonight thanks to three goals in the first half. The first came from a Christian Pulisic header, the second was an Adrien Rabiot goal from a corner and the third was a Diego Moreira free-kick.

Alessandro Bastoni’s goal had briefly halved the deficit, but it was to be all for nothing as Milan racked up their fourth Derby della Madonnina win in a row. It moves the Rossoneri four points behind their city rivals, and also ends their unbeaten start to the season.

Pulisic spoke to DAZN after the full-time whistle to give his assessments on the game, and his words were relayed by MilanNews.

“We started the match very well, with intensity, with physicality. We played very well, scoring two goals in the first part, and this victory is very important for us.”

Four games, four goals, and four wins with Inter…

“I have to keep scoring in the derby, yes (laughs, ed.)”

“These are three very important points for us, but we have to continue to find this consistency and win every match.”

“Yes, we always play well in big games like today, so it’s not a surprise to me. We did things well.”

#1876. Mikel Arteta sends clear message to £60million Chelsea transfer target

Mikel Arteta has assured one of his out of favour stars that he remains a key part of his plans.

The Gunners have made a superb start to their Premier League title defence, winning eight of their nine games so far and put down a significant marker last weekend with first win at Anfield in 14 years.

Arteta’s side have made an equally impressive start to their European campaign and extended their unbeaten run following a 2-2 draw at the home of German champions Bayern Munich a fortnight ago.

Arsenal’s excellence has come at a cost, however, with several high-profile players struggling for significant game time.

#1875. Manchester United injury update: Carlos Baleba, Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw latest news and return dates

Manchester United’s winless run was finally snapped before it got to ten matches on Tuesday as pressure eased on Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils looked as though they were beaten by Roma at Old Trafford in what would have been the latest plunge in their recent plight, but Matheus Cunha’s late double turned the game on its head to earn a dramatic 3-2 victory.

United suffered a fresh injury blow in that defeat, while fans vented their anger in the direction of the directors’ box, protesting the club’s ownership with balloons and tennis balls during the tie.

With that in mind, here is all the latest Manchester United injury news and potential return dates...

The summer signing had been a rare shining light in what has otherwise been a miserable campaign for United so far.

The Cameroonian started alongside Kobbie Mainoo in the engine room for the first time, but saw his game curtailed just moments into the second half.

He pulled up in agony holding his hamstring, and was forced off immediately.

Post-match, Carrick said of the midfielder: “I haven't got any more news on Carlos at this stage, but obviously it looks like it's his hamstring," Carrick said.

"So we'll just have to assess what that looks like. I mean, initially, it doesn't look great. Timelines? I haven't got much more to give you."

The England forward has been struggling with a niggling hip problem in recent weeks.

There had been hope that he could return to action against Chelsea or Roma, but he was in the squad for neither game.

Carrick mentioned ahead of the Roma clash that he would be closing in on a comeback this week, which could point towards a return this weekend.

Potential return date: Saturday, November 7 vs Aston Villa (H)

Left-back Shaw is still sidelined with a muscluar problem that he picked up in the 1-1 draw with Tottenham.

The Slovenian saw his debut season cut short by the injury, and he missed the start to this term with a similar problem.

It emerged last week that he would now be out for a further, elongated period.

“He's going to be out for a period of time,” Carrick said before the defeat by Chelsea. “We're not exactly sure yet how long, but it's going to be a significant amount of time, unfortunately.

“So I feel for Ben, he had the issue at the end of last season that we looked after and tried to give him as much time to recover and then unfortunately he's had the issue coming into this season.

“So, we've got to do what's best for Ben and he's going to have to have some time on the sidelines, unfortunately.

“It's not great for us, it's certainly not great for Ben, but it is part of the game and we've just got to try and make the best of it and get him back as quick as we can.”

Uruguay international Ugarte is set to be out for much of this season with a torn ACL that he sustained at the World Cup.

#1874. Jamie O’Hara blasts ‘atrocious’ Manchester United star after Roma win

Jamie O’Hara branded Diogo Dalot ‘atrocious’ after Manchester United’s incredible comeback win over Roma in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s struggling side came from 2-0 down to clinch an unlikely 3-2 win over Serie A side Roma at Old Trafford.

Manchester United, enduring their worst start to a season since the 1980s, went behind after just 11 minutes as Matias Soule took advantage of space left by the absent Dalot to fire past Senne Lammens.

Dalot was out of position again five minutes later as Ayden Heaven blocked a shot with his arm to give Roma a penalty which was converted by Donyell Malen.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The home side were once again booed off and Michael Carrick was surely heading for the sack until United produced a brilliant second-half comeback.

Bruno Fernandes got the Red Devils back in the game with a retaken penalty won by Matheus Cunha, who then scored two late goals to stun the Italians and spark bedlam at Old Trafford.

O’Hara praised Manchester United’s unlikely comeback but said the team were ‘pathetic’ in the first-half and was particularly critical of ‘atrocious’ Portugal international Dalot.

‘We were watching the Manchester United game and the first-half was pathetic, we were in shock at how bad they were,’ O’Hara said on talkSPORT.

‘They could have been 4-0 down. But in the second half they turned it around and they were fantastic, they put in a big performance in the end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But they were pathetic in the first-half, it was so open and they stopped running, they had given up. They were gone, they were done.

THAT DIDN'T TAKE LONG 😬United fall behind after just 11 minutes as Roma score through Matías Soulé 🇦🇷 pic.twitter.com/DtIOFJYZ6D

‘Roma should have absolutely buried them but they didn’t. They were all over the place at the back. Dalot… oh my god.

‘I said during the first-half, they have to take him off, he was atrocious. I don’t know what he was doing, I don’t know. It was awful defending, it was so bad. I couldn’t believe how bad they were.’

Carrick praised his players for their response in the second-half and urged them to take that momentum into United’s dismal Premier League campaign.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United are just 17th in the top-flight, two points above bottom-placed Sunderland, ahead of Sunday’s clash against Aston Villa.

‘It was a good night,’ Carrick told Amazon Prime. ‘I have to give credit to the players, I think we grew into it after giving the goals away.

‘The boys made every little bit of every opportunity. We were brilliant in the end. It’s one game though, it depends what happens next and we have to show that.

‘It’s a win for us as a football club and we get to send the fans home happy. We have to make the most of it. I don’t have a crystal ball to know what happens next.

‘We move on to the weekend. We’ve got a really important game here against Aston Villa, which we need to prepare for right.’

Meanwhile, Manchester United captain Fernandes said the win was not about saving Carrick his job.

‘We don’t need to save anyone’s job,’ he insisted. ‘The club needed that win, the players needed that win.

‘We have been working so hard to get out of this situation all together. It’s been tough but it doesn’t change the belief I have of the manager and the staff and every player in this club.

‘It doesn’t change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me.’

United’s next opponents Aston Villa are 10th in the Premier League and lost 3-0 to Champions League contenders Barcelona on Tuesday night.

#1871. How to watch Fenerbahce vs Liverpool: TV channel and live stream for Champions League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Liverpool will be reunited with a familiar face for this evening’s Champions League clash against Fenerbahce.

After Ismail Kartal resigned from his Fenerbahce post last week, Dirk Kuyt has been installed as the Turkish side’s interim boss which means he will face the club he played for between 2006 and 2012.

The Dutchman has got his work cut out to get Fenerbahce firing in this season’s league phase, having been thumped 6-0 by Aston Villa on matchday two and drawing with Roma and Slavia Prague.

Speaking in the pre-match press conference, Kuyt admitted he will need to keep his emotions in check for what he describes as an “special occasion”.

He said: "Of course, tomorrow will be a very special occasion for me but at the stage we're in, I'm not here for myself. I'm here for the club and that's what is important - to show the fans who deserve much more, a reaction, positive energy and a good performance."

Liverpool, meanwhile, have won all three games in the league phase so far, scoring 12 goals but have conceded seven as Andoni Iraola has not yet struck the right balance between attack and defence.

The Reds are seeking to bounce back from defeat to Arsenal at the weekend, though they can take confidence from the fact that they have won four of five away games across all competitions this season.

While Liverpool are no strangers to Turkey, particularly Istanbul, this will be the first-ever meeting with Fenerbahce at any level and the attacking talent across both squads suggests an entertaining game is on the cards.

Here’s everything you need to know about where to watch the match...

TV channel: You can watch this game in the UK on TNT Sports 1, with coverage set to start at 5pm GMT ahead of the 5.45pm GMT kick-off.

#1870. Gallery: ‘Milan in ecstasy’, ‘A masterclass from Amorim’ – Today’s front pages in Italy

AC Milan pulled off a Halloween spectacular at San Siro last night as they beat city rivals Inter 3-1 in the derby.

All four goals came in the first half, with Christian Pulisic’s header and Adrien Rabiot’s flick from a corner putting Milan in dreamland less than 10 minutes in. Alessandro Bastoni halved the deficit, before Diego Moreira’s outstanding free-kick restored the two-goal lead.

It was a result that the Rossoneri badly needed after the midweek setback against Bologna, and it shows the level that they are capable of playing at. Below is how the Italian newspapers have reacted.

La Gazzetta dello Sport: “Milan in ecstasy. The derby remains a nightmare for Inter. Moreira is king: two assists and a goal. Chivu, in a crisis situation, falls short. Amorim dominates, Cardinale emotional: ‘Unbelievable’.”

Corriere dello Sport: “Stramorim. Ruben dismantles Chivu’s side. Moreira puts on a masterclass: within the first 10 minutes, the Belgian provides the assists for goals by Pulisic and Rabiot. Bastoni offers a glimmer of hope, but Maignan stands like a wall. Then, a moment of magic from Diego via a free-kick. Milan move to within 4 points of the top.”

Tuttosport: “Devilish. A rampant Milan leave Inter reeling. It’s Moreira’s night: he provides assists for Pulisic and Rabiot, then conjures a moment of magic from a free- kick, following a goal from Bastoni.”

“A masterclass from Amorim, while this time Chivu fails to engineer a comeback; it’s their first league defeat, and Lazio could pull away today. The derby nightmare continues: that’s now eight games without a win for the Nerazzurri.”
