#1855. Chivu still striving for consistency after Inter’s victory over Feyenoord

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Cristian Chivu insisted that consistency would be key to achieving what Inter are trying to build this season following their victory over Feyenoord in the Champions League.

Inter arrived into Tuesday's clash at Stadion Feijenoord on the back of a 3-1 defeat to AC Milan in the Derby della Madonnina, which was their first Serie A loss of the season.

But they responded with a 3-0 win over Feyenoord, with Yann Bisseck, Francesco Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski all on target against their Eredivisie opponents.

Chivu's side took the lead in the eighth minute when Bisseck picked out the bottom left corner before Esposito's header struck the crossbar and found its way past Tjark Ernst.

Zielinski added to Inter's advantage nine minutes after the restart as the Serie A giants registered their 87th win in the Champions League, drawing level with rivals Milan for the joint-second most of any Italian club, only Juventus have more (118).

Inter also remain unbeaten across their 14 Champions League meetings with Dutch sides (W11 D3), with this 3-0 win being their biggest against a Dutch club in the competition.

Cesc Fabregas' Como are up next in their next Serie A outing, and Chivu is hoping the confidence-boosting win over Feyenoord gives his team the momentum they need to get back to winning ways in the league.

"Consistency is what brings results, it gives you self-confidence and belief in what you are doing, it is what we are looking for at this moment," Chivu told Sky Sport Italia, as quoted by Football Italia.

"This game gives us a big boost of confidence in what we are building, so we know football can take you down some strange paths, but you must be able to react and get back onto the right path."

RETURNING TO MILANO WITH THREE POINTS IN THE https://t.co/vkWHVXvwoA

Inter had been criticised for their bad starts in recent matches, with this the first time they had taken the lead as early as the eighth minute since August.

Bisseck's strike saw him score his first goal in the Champions League (27th appearance), becoming just the second German player to score for Inter in the competition, after Robin Gosens against Barcelona in October 2022.

It was assisted by Djed Spence, who registered his first goal involvement in any club competition since April 2025, ending a 58-game run without a goal contribution. He also became the first English player to either score or assist for Inter in the Champions League.

And Chivu believes Inter were "the best version of ourselves" against Feyenoord, adding: "We have certain values, we understand certain things and put them on the pitch.

"That doesn't mean we haven't done well so far this season.

"We tried to be the best version of ourselves, it worked with organisation, intensity and everything we needed for a strong performance in a stadium that is not easy to play in.

"We always have discussions after every game, whether it goes well or badly, we try to correct errors and build on our strengths.

"Sometimes it goes better than others, perhaps we understood what wasn't going on as well.

"The Inter world, the club owners, the fans, we are all aware of the values of these players who want to fly the flag high. That has never been in doubt."

#1854. Monaco vs Nordsjaelland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 02 Nov 2026 22:28, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:51

Monaco will put their 100% record in the Conference League on the line Thursday as they return to the Principality to face Nordsjaelland at Stade Louis II.

After two matchdays, Les Monegasques are tied for first on points, having defeated Freiburg 3-0 the last time out, while Nordsjaelland sit 19th after a 2-2 draw with CSKA Sofia.

While their form has dropped a little domestically, Monaco have yet to falter in Europe, winning all four of their games in this competition so far.

However, Filipe Luis has seen his side go winless in their last three Ligue 1 affairs, netting just one goal over that stretch.

On the other hand, they sit third in the Conference League regarding average goals conceded per match (0.5), with only Brighton & Hove Albion and St. Truiden doing better (0).

At home, this team have been especially sharp defensively this season, conceding a goal or fewer in five of their six matches played at Stade Louis II across all competitions.

Monaco have netted three or more times in both of their home games in this competition so far and can stretch their unbeaten run in the League Phase of a European tournament to seven matchdays on Thursday.

This will mark the first time they face a side from Denmark in Europe, with Les Monegasques winning their only European match this decade against a Scandinavian opponent, blanking Bodo/Glimt 1-0 in Norway in last season’s Champions League.

They continue to seek that elusive first triumph in this edition of the Conference League, but Nordsjaelland have shown plenty of resilience in the League Phase this time around.

Jens Fonsskov Olsen’s men have come back from 1-0 down in both of their group matches to earn a point, putting them just a point above the knockout line heading into matchday three.

Thursday will be their first-ever meeting versus a Ligue 1 side in Europe, as they seek a first victory in the League Phase of this tournament since hammering Fenerbahce 6-1 in Denmark in 2023.

Their last away victory in this competition came in Slovakia that same year against Spartak Trnava (2-0), while they are currently on a four-game unbeaten run as the visitors across all competitions.

The Danes have never lost a Conference League affair in this portion of the competition when netting first, dropping points only once in that scenario.

On Thursday, they could suffer consecutive competitive defeats for the first time all season after losing 3-2 domestically versus Midtjylland on Sunday.

Hamstring injuries will likely keep Stanis Idumbo and Ansu Fati out of the Monaco fold on matchday three, while Eric Dier should be available after recently recovering from a thigh strain.

Paris Brunner has two goals for Les Monegasques in this phase of the tournament, with the German netting the winner against Freiburg on matchday two, while Lamine Camara and Ansu Fati also scored on that occasion.

An ankle issue may keep Noah Markmann on the Nordsjaelland sidelines for this one, Victor Nelsson has a sore shoulder, Tobias Salquist is dealing with fitness problems, while Jakob Busk and Souleymane Alio have knocks and Justin Janssen is suspended.

Ibrahim Adel netted a brace against Sofia, as he now leads the team in this competition thanks to those two strikes.

Hradecky; Vanderson, Teze, Dier, Mawissa; Zakaria, Camara; Minamino, Golovin, Detourbet; Brunner

Hansen; Acquah, Tuka, Norheim; Heyde, Brink, Rojkjaer, Lahteenmaki; Berthelsen, Lind, Adel

We expect the Danes to play conservatively and hang back, trying to hold off the Principality club throughout the match.

Monaco, however, are usually at their best offensively at home, and we believe they can dominate this game and eventually break down Nordsjaelland, who have not faced a side with as much attacking depth as Les Monegasques.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal face Slavia Prague in the Champions League tonight, with William Saliba closing in on a return and Max Dowman pushing to start.

Dowman was absent from the Gunners’ 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield as he started a three-match suspension following his late sending off in the Carabao Cup defeat by Fleetwood.

Saliba travelled with the squad on Tuesday afternoon as he pushes to show that he is ready to make his first appearance of the season.

#1851. Manchester United co-owners INEOS sack manager as official statement released

INEOS have sacked Lausanne-Sport manager Luka Elsner after just five months in charge, amid ongoing pressure on Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick.

The Swiss club, which is part-owned by Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS group, confirmed on Tuesday that they had mutually agreed to end their relationship with the 44-year-old.

Elsner was appointed on 1 June but struggled to make an impact, winning eight of his 12 Swiss Super League matches. Lausanne's poor start to the campaign left them bottom of the table, prompting the club to make a change.

A statement read: “After lengthy discussions about the current sporting situation, FC Lausanne-Sport and Luka Elsner have mutually agreed to end their collaboration.”

His departure comes at a difficult time for INEOS at Manchester United, where Carrick is facing scrutiny following a disappointing run of results.

United's supporters have made their frustration with the club's ownership clear in recent weeks, directing criticism towards Ratcliffe and the Glazer family.

Protests continued during Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Roma, when fans threw green and gold balloons on to the pitch in the 21st minute while chanting against the owners.

The atmosphere improved after United produced a second-half comeback to secure a 3-2 victory. Bruno Fernandes scored from the penalty spot before Matheus Cunha struck twice to complete the turnaround.

However, the result is unlikely to remove the pressure on Carrick, who remains under scrutiny as United attempt to improve their domestic form.

The decision to part company with Elsner after such a short period is also likely to attract attention given INEOS' involvement in both clubs.

#1850. Cardiff City vs West Ham United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 02 Nov 2026 22:36, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:59

West Ham United will be looking to bounce back from consecutive defeats when they head to South Wales for Wednesday's Championship clash against Cardiff City.

The managerless Hammers head into the midweek round of fixtures in eighth position, while Cardiff are currently sitting in 17th spot in the Championship table.

Cardiff, who won promotion from League One last term, are sitting five points above the drop zone after winning three, drawing five and losing five of their 13 league games this season.

The Bluebirds recently enjoyed a three-game unbeaten run that saw them record home wins against Watford and Birmingham City, on either side of an away draw against Middlesbrough.

However, their encouraging run of form was brought to a disappointing end by Saturday's 3-0 loss against Wolverhampton Wanderers at Molineux, extending their wait for their first away win of the season.

Having mustered just two points from seven road trips, Brian Barry-Murphy's side will be looking forward to returning to the Cardiff City Stadium, especially as they are one of four teams yet to lose a Championship home game this term (W3, D3).

In fact, they have won each of their last three home games, scoring nine goals and conceding on just two occasions in that winning run.

They will be hoping to produce another strong performance in front of their supporters in their first meeting with West Ham since picking up a 2-0 victory in March 2019 - a result that ended a seven-game losing run in head-to-head encounters.

West Ham may be sitting inside the top eight, but after the Hammers won just two of their last six matches (D2, L2), Nuno Espirito Santo was given the boot on Tuesday morning.

The Hammers are in need of a confidence boost after losing back-to-back league matches for the first time since being relegated from the Premier League, and managerial favourite Scott Parker could soon provide that amid suggestions that he will soon replace Nuno.

West Ham shipped three goals in the first half of the 3-2 loss against the Saints, before they fell to a 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion at the weekend, leaving them four points adrift of automatic promotion.

The visitors can at least take comfort from the fact that they will head on their travels with the only unbeaten away record in the Championship after recording three wins and three draws from their six road trips.

In fact, they are looking to claim a third consecutive away win without conceding after beating Lincoln City 6-0 and Swansea City 1-0 in their last two away assignments.

The visitors certainly possess the firepower to take three points from Wednesday's away, having racked up 33 goals in 13 league games this term - at least three more than any other side ahead of the midweek round of fixtures.

Cardiff are experiencing a defensive injury crisis, with Barry-Murphy unable to call upon the suspended Gabriel Osho and the injured trio of Dylan Lawlor, Callum Chambers and Krystian Bielik.

Will Fish is a doubt after sustaining a hamstring problem against Wolves, while Perry Ng may have to battle through his own fitness issues to help his side in Wednesday's fixture.

Midfielder Alex Robertson is also an injury concern after being taken off in Saturday's defeat with an Achilles problem.

As for the visitors, Konstantinos Mavropanos will miss a second straight game with a knee injury he sustained in the defeat to Southampton.

Interim coaches Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville are also without Venezuela international Keiber Lamadrid, who has not featured in any of the last eight matchday squads due to a knee problem.

The West Ham coaching team could make several changes to their starting lineup, with Joel Veltman, Tomas Soucek, Manor Solomon and Taty Castellanos among those in contention to feature at the Cardiff City Stadium.

#1849. England captain Harry Kane reveals whether he would swap Ballon d'Or for Champions League trophy

By Ben Sully | 02 Nov 2026 23:34, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 04:09

Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane has admitted he would trade his Ballon d'Or for Champions League glory.

Last week, Kane became the first Englishman to win the prestigious Ballon d'Or award after fending off competition from Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal.

Kane was recognised after scoring 61 goals in 51 competitive matches for Bayern last term, as well as netting six goals in England's World Cup campaign.

The 33-year-old has won multiple individual honours throughout his career and has claimed five trophies during his time in Germany, including two Bundesliga titles.

However, like Mbappe and Yamal, he is still waiting to get his prize on the biggest club trophy in European football, the Champions League.

Kane, who is set to lead the Bayern line against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, provided an honest answer when asked which trophy he would choose between the Ballon d'Or and the Champions League.

"Team trophies are why we play football, the team aspect of our sport is really, really important," Kane told reporters on Monday.

"The Ballon d'Or last week was one of the best feelings I've had in my life and my career.

"But to have moments with the team, celebrations with the club, to be able to lift the Champions League with Bayern would be an incredible feeling.

"I would choose the Champions League, but I have the opportunity to do both - let's see what happens.

"The Ballon d'Or is a highlight, it puts me on an even bigger level, but you want to have these big finals, the Champions League, having that feeling of emotion with your teammates as well."

Tuesday's Champions League fixture between Bayern and Atletico will take place at the ground where Kane came closest to winning the European Cup.

The striker played the full duration of Tottenham Hotspur's 2-0 defeat to Liverpool in the 2018-19 Champions League final at the Metropolitano.

Kane has made two semi-final appearances since joining Bayern, including a narrow 6-5 aggregate defeat against Paris Saint-Germain in last season's Champions League.

Vincent Kompany's side certainly has the talent to make another deep run in the competition and is seen as one of the teams that could seriously challenge for the trophy.

However, their chances of winning may depend on the form and fitness of key players, like Kane, Luis Diaz, Michael Olise, and Joshua Kimmich.

Kane will most likely need to produce a similar European campaign to last season's return of 14 goals in 13 matches, including six goals in five knockout-round appearances.

#1848. Flick thrilled to end Barcelona’s clean-sheet drought against Aston Villa

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Hansi Flick said the most impressive aspect of Barcelona's 3-0 win over Aston Villa in the Champions League was the performance of his defenders to earn a rare clean sheet.

Barcelona returned to winning ways in the competition at the Camp Nou on Tuesday, with Lamine Yamal's seventh-minute strike laying the foundations for their triumph.

Yamal capitalised on Joao Gomes' risky pass across his own goal before picking out the bottom-left corner, which proved to be a record-breaking strike.

The 19-year-old became the teenager with the most goals in Champions League history (14), surpassing the previous record, set by Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe (13).

And two goals in 12 minutes after the break from Barcelona captain Raphinha sealed the win, but it was at the other end where Flick felt his team deserved the most praise.

Barcelona picked up their first clean sheet in the Champions League since a 4-0 win over Borussia Dortmund in April 2025, ending a run of 18 games without one, while they have now won 11 of their last 13 home games in the competition against English clubs (D2).

They limited Unai Emery's team to an expected goals (xG) total of just 0.72 from their nine attempts, with only one of those forcing Joan Garcia into making a save.

"The best thing about the match? The clean sheet. I'm very happy with that because we defended a very good attack like Aston Villa's," Flick told reporters.

"Of course, it was important. They are a great team. We defended well, and we were happy with what we saw in defence.

"Everyone gave their maximum to finish with a clean sheet and we scored our goals. We're pleased."

A great win at home, Hansi! https://t.co/V1qqYCM81G

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 4, 2026

Barcelona have now failed to score in just one of their previous 20 home games in the Champions League (W15 D2 L3), netting 65 goals in that time (3.3 per game).

The Blaugrana have also had at least five big chances in each of their last three Champions League games for the first time since December 2020.

It was a result that saw Barcelona inflict Villa's joint-heaviest defeat in major European competition, having also lost by three goals to Royal Antwerp in September 1975 (1-4) and Inter in November 1990 (0-3), both in the UEFA Cup.

And Villa's downfall was from their own making after Gomes' mistake for Yamal's goal. No Premier League side has committed more errors leading to goals in all competitions this season than the Villans (seven, level with Sunderland).

Flick, however, said that Barcelona's opener was something they had worked on, explaining: "This is our idea of how we want to play football.

"We try to press them high, so that they make mistakes. We had this moment, were in the right position, and we pressed them well, and they made this mistake and we used it."

Flick was also on hand to explain his decision behind replacing Rodri for Marc Bernal at half-time, with the Barcelona boss citing a slight injury problem for the Spaniard.

"We took him off at half-time because he felt some muscular pain. It'll need to wait until Wednesday before we examine that and find out more," Flick said.

No decision has been made over his future, but a potential departure could develop sooner than expected.

West Ham have sacked Nuno Espirito Santo as head coach.

A statement reads: “West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espirito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

“Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

“Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

“West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

“The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway.”

#1846. Big game players, big game performances: Player ratings for Milan-Inter from Italian papers

Last night’s win against Inter was proof of the quality within the AC Milan squad, so now it’s a case of continuing on the path upwards.

For Milan, a win in the derby wasn’t essential. Yes, it would always be a big help, but avoiding defeat was the priority, given a 10-point gap would’ve opened to the title leaders. Yet, the Rossoneri were brave and fought for three points, even if most would’ve taken one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A defining performance of the Ruben Amorim era so far, everyone played their role stupendously – and that includes the Portuguese, who tactically outclassed his counterpart. As a result, the scores from us were rather high in our post-match ratings.

Looking at the ratings from elsewhere, Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) gave the performance an eight, also giving Amorim that score, too.

In terms of the players’ performances, Goncalo Ramos was the lowest, with a still passable score of a 6. However, Ardon Jashari and Davide Bartesaghi were also given these scores, understandable after coming off the bench.

With 6.5s, Koni De Winter, Yunus Musah and Alphadjo Cisse were all very solid, with the latter almost grabbing a fourth in the game. Mario Gila, Strahinja Pavlovic and Sankhoun Diawara were given 7s, as did Luka Modric and the first goalscorer Christian Pulisic.

The Diavolo’s French duo – Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot – were awarded a score of 7.5, whilst Diego Moreira was given an eight for his goal and two assists.

Moving to Corriere dello Sport, Amorim was given an eight again. Ramos scored the lowest again, at a six, whilst Musah, Diawara, Pavlovic and De Winter were given 6.5. Gila, Modric, Pulisic and Rabiot were given 7s. Then, Maignan was given a 7.5, Moreira, again, was given an 8/10.

Finally, Tuttosport’s ratings were largely the same. Ramos was given a downgrade to a 5/10, whilst Moreira was given another eight. The French goalkeeper kept his second-best position with a 7.5 – alongside Rabiot – thanks to his big saves, whilst Diawara was also given a bump up to a 7, thanks to an impressive derby debut.

Elsewhere, Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Musah and Pulisic were given 6.5s, Modric played a 7/10 game and Amorim was given a 7.5.

#1845. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

Newcastle have just about got past West Brom, winning 3-2 in the end, and they book their place in the third round.

At least the travelling Charlton fans have something to cheer about even if their side are being dumped out of the League Cup. A corner from the left comes to the back post, where Jones rises highest to head it between Kinsky’s legs and into the Tottenham net.

Savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

The Brazilian signed just yesterday but he now has a first Tottenham goal to his name. He cuts inside from the right and drives across the face of the penalty area before firing at the near post, beating Brooks. Tottenham are cruising into the third round and their newest signing scores on his debut.

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Change for Tottenham as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel.

Tel crosses from the left side of the box and picks out Savio, who attempts an audacious flick that does not come off.

West Brom were not back on level terms for long as Barnes has his second of the game and Newcastle lead 3-2 with under 10 minutes remaining.

Charlton have barely threatened the Tottenham goal tonight but that is a decent opportunity for Leaburn, who is played in down the right and forces Kinsky into a decent save.

Savio is straight into the action with good work down the right and squares it for Tel, whose shot is straight at Brooks.

Savio is on for his Tottenham debut and replaces Solanke. Savio only joined Tottenham yesterday but makes his first appearance for the club tonight.

Price has stepped up to score his second of the game to bring West Brom level at 2-2 with just over 10 minutes to go.

The Austrian defender has just come on and, with his first touch, puts Tottenham 3-0 up. Fernandes’ free-kick from just outside the box on the right is met by Danso, who attacks it and his header finds the bottom corner. You have to say that goal was coming. Danso has hurt himself as there was a clash of heads as he met the delivery and receives treatment to his head.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

Roberto De Zerbi is turning to his bench and making a triple change as Van de Ven, Danso and Porro come on.

Charlton are also making a triple change of their own.

Gray is found on the left side of the Charlton penalty area and he drives his shot towards goal, forcing Brooks into a decent save. Tottenham are pushing for that third goal.

A cross is sent in from the right and it comes to Tel, who volleys first time but it is a fairly routine save for Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Tottenham are starting to ramp up the pressure as they go in search of a third goal. As it stands, the only side that looks like scoring is Tottenham.

Plenty of cheers from the home fans as Savio is out to warm up. Will Roberto De Zerbi turn to the Brazilian and give him his debut tonight?

One of the new laws brought in this season is to speed up throw-ins and Gray falls foul of taking too long, with Charlton then being given the throw-in.

Tel decides to shoot from range after Charlton clear a corner but the Frenchman’s effort is straight at Brooks

Play has resumed in north London, with Tottenham 2-0 up over Charlton.

They are back under way at St James’ Park and there has been a goal within a few minutes of the second half starting. Newcastle were 1-0 down against West Brom but they now lead 2-1 thanks to Barnes’ goal.

Possession: Tottenham 76%-24% CharltonShots: 9-2Shots on target: 4-1Corners: 7-2Touches in opposition box: 25-2

The first half in north London is brought to an end and Tottenham take a 2-0 lead into the break thanks to goals from Moore and Solanke. Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

Whilst they are still in added time in north London, it is half-time at St James’ Park and Newcastle are level 1-1 with West Brom.

Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

Due to a few Charlton injuries, there will be six added minutes.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Tottenham have their second just before the break. Charlton fail to clear their lines inside their own box before Solanke volleys in on the swivel from the penalty spot. Charlton will feel that was definitely an avoidable goal.

Tottenham had looked rather lethargic but they take the lead in emphatic style. The 19-year-old cuts inside from the right and comes across the face of the Charlton penalty area. Moore then strikes it powerfully with his left foot and the ball flies into the roof of the net. Could Brooks have done better in the Charlton goal? Moore will not care.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

Tottenham are currently too slow in possession and are not moving the ball quickly enough, meaning it is easier for Charlton to defend.

West Brom had taken the lead at St James’ Park but Newcastle are back on level terms through summer signing Toure.

A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

Solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

Charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the hosts as Bergvall cynically takes down Apter as the Charlton man drove towards the Tottenham penalty area. You feel like Charlton need to take advantage of opportunities like this if they want to win this tie. The ball is clipped in and it comes off Van Hecke’s head for a corner. Tottenham clear their lines initially but Charlton keep it alive. Docherty strikes it first time from the edge of the Tottenham box and forces Kinsky into a good save diving to his left.

That probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

Roberto De Zerbi was keen to see his side show a reaction to their defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Unsurprisingly, they are dominating possession but have not posed much of a threat going forward.

There has been a goal at St James’ Park and it is the visitors West Brom who have taken the lead over Newcastle. Price has scored directly from a free-kick and the Championship side lead.

A sensational free-kick from Isaac Price to give West Brom the lead at St. James' Park! 🤯Watch the Carabao Cup here! - https://t.co/4BMyhp9stB pic.twitter.com/Pnt78LWFN6

Things have just gone from bad to worse for Charlton. Whilst one of their centre-backs is being stretchered off in Sichenje, their other centre-half Koumetio, who used to be on the books at Liverpool, is also down. Koumetio, like Sichenje, is going to come off. McNamara and Jones, who like Koumetio used to be at Liverpool, are coming on. Charlton have had to change both centre-backs inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Sichenje did try to continue but he has gone back down again and his night appears to be over. The question will be has he done more damage to his knee trying to play on? The stretcher is being brought on and it will be a sorry end to his night.

Moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

Sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

Play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and we are just moments away from kick-off north London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1844. Will William Saliba play tonight? Arsenal latest team news as defender returns from injury

Arsenal fans will have been thrilled by the sight of William Saliba walking out onto grass at the club’s London Colney training ground on Tuesday.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal triple raid; Man Utd want Bellingham

Arsenal XI vs Slavia Prague: Predicted lineup and confirmed team news

How to watch Slavia Prague vs Arsenal: TV channel and live stream

The centre-back has returned to full training after three and a half months on the sidelines, having been out of action with a back problem that required an extended period of rehabilitation rather than surgery.

In Saliba’s absence, £55million summer signing Ezri Konsa has been a more-than-capable deputy alongside Gabriel.

But Saliba has forged an impressive, years-long centre-back partnership with Gabriel that was crucial to Arsenal winning the Premier League title last season.

So, Arsenal fans will be keen to see Saliba in action as soon as possible, and could he take to the pitch tonight against Slavia Prague in the Champions League?

Saliba took part in Tuesday's session, before manager Mikel Arteta told a pre-match press conference that the defender "is in a really good place."

The France defender joined his team-mates on the plane flying to Prague, so can be named in the matchday squad should Arteta deem him ready.

He added: "His evolution has been as expected, which is not always the case. He feels very comfortable. He played 45 minutes behind closed doors last week.

“He feels ready to go now, so whether we use him or not is a matter of what the team needs."

But, have almost four months out, Saliba may not be rushed back into the team.

Konsa has delivered a series of fine performances, and Arteta might prove reluctant to disrupt that partnership just yet.

Switching Konsa to right-back offers one option, given he occasionally played there for former club Aston Villa and England.

Arteta also has Jurrien Timber and Ben White as right-back options.

Asked whether having all three centre-backs available was a "problem", Arteta laughed and remarked: "So far we haven't had that luxury. I wouldn't call it a problem.

"We are going to have the opportunity to ... manage the congestion of the players in a much better way than we have actually done it."

#1843. Simeone: Atletico still a level below Europe’s elite

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Diego Simeone conceded that Atletico Madrid were still behind some of Europe's elite teams after being beaten 2-0 by Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Simeone watched on as his side slipped to a second defeat in this year's competition, with second-half strikes from Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer sealing the victory.

But Atletico had their chances in the first half, with Julian Alvarez firing just wide before Pablo Barrios saw his goal-bound effort deflect over Manuel Neuer's crossbar.

However, Bayern took the lead in the 54th minute through Karl, who capitalised on Robin Le Normand's hesitancy in his own penalty area before finishing past Jan Oblak.

The Bundesliga giants sealed the win when Harry Kane's pass over the top picked out Laimer, who was allowed time and space to bring down the ball before firing into the roof of the net, with none of Atletico's defenders closing down the Bayern full-back.

Atletico have now won just one of their last seven Champions League games (D2 L4) after winning three of the four before that (L1), leaving them 22nd in the 36-team standings.

Simeone's side have also kept just two clean sheets in their last 17 home European games after chalking up 17 shutouts in the 28 before that, and the Atletico boss acknowledged that teams such as Bayern were on another level at this moment in time.

"We know that when we play against important opponents it can happen," Simeone told reporters.

"Liverpool and Bayern are better than us, we have to get closer to them. We have to reach 120 because 100 is not going to reach us."

When asked about what he would learn from the defeat, Simeone added: "We managed it well. Sorloth's presence helped us.

"We could bet on a more direct game by winning the second ball. He gave us a lot. The match was on that side.

"We played it the way we wanted, but the first goal came, and we didn't know how to react. With the second goal, the game ended."

— Atlético de Madrid (@atletienglish) November 3, 2026

Atletico had come into the clash with confidence following their 2-0 win over Levante in LaLiga.

Saturday's triumph saw Atletico record their seventh consecutive league win, the longest active streak across Europe's top five leagues.

Neither Atletico nor Bayern managed a shot on target in the first half, the first time both sides in a Champions League game have drawn a first-half blank since January 2025 (Club Brugge v Juventus), but it was the visitors who had the better chances.

Bayern finished the first half with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.08 from their nine shots, while Atletico registered a tally of 0.37 from their four attempts before the break.

Atletico were only able to bump their xG up to 1.02 in the second half compared to Bayern's 1.91, and Alexander Sorloth said his team could not keep up with their opponents.

"Bayern are one of the best teams in the world. In the first half, we defended well, we had some opportunities, and we only missed the final pass," Sorloth added.

"So the first half was decent, but in the second half we got tired. We did not have the legs and Bayern scored.

"Of course, we wanted to have more points than this, but we have four games left. Every time we go out onto the pitch we want to win. We hope to win our final games."

Sorloth's comments were echoed by Marcos Llorente, who said: "We knew what kind of game we were in for.

"They're a very strong team; we were holding our own, but it's the little things that decide the game, and we didn't expect that first goal.

"It came down to the little things – not staying calm enough on that final pass, not rushing, and being more aggressive in attack by getting players into the box."

#1842. Fenerbahce vs Liverpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 02 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 12:48

Fighting to maintain their 100% start in the Champions League's league-phase, Liverpool will travel to face Fenerbahce at Sukru Saracoglu Stadium on Wednesday.

The Yellow Canaries are in dire form ahead of this high-profile clash, and the Reds will be hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out.

Fenerbahce are currently under the leadership of interim manager Dirk Kuyt, a familiar face to Liverpool fans, following Ismail Kartal's resignation last month.

The Dutchman spent six years at Anfield, scoring 71 goals across 285 appearances, but will be vying to end his former club's continental winning streak.

Kuyt took the reins on October 28 after the Yellow Canaries were downed 2-1 by bitter rivals Galatasaray, but fell to a 2-1 defeat of his own against Goztepe on Saturday.

While the boss is waiting for an inaugural positive result, Fenerbahce are also searching for their first win in this season's Champions League, having drawn 1-1 with Roma and 2-2 with Slavia Prague either side of a 6-0 demolition by Aston Villa.

While the hosts come into Wednesday's showdown as the underdogs, fans will cling to the fact that the Istanbul club have only tasted defeat in one of their last five home matches as a reason for optimism.

Meanwhile, Liverpool seem to have found their feet under Andoni Iraola, though they will need to show character to recover after a disappointing defeat at the weekend.

In the aftermath of their 3-0 loss to Manchester City on October 11, the Reds racked up five consecutive wins across all competitions, including a 2-0 victory over high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion and a penalty shootout triumph against Chelsea in the EFL Cup.

Iraola's side also collected six points from six in the Champions League during that run, thanks to a 6-3 win over LASK and a dramatic 4-3 comeback against Villarreal on October 20.

However, Arsenal claimed their first league success at Anfield for 14 years on Sunday, beating the Merseysiders 1-0 in controversial fashion, a result that perhaps laid Liverpool's limitations against deep blocks bare.

That being said, Wednesday's visitors are undefeated away from home throughout 2026-27, winning four times and drawing once, scoring 13 goals in the process.

Already in a strong position - third in the Champions League table with nine points - another victory would solidify the Premier League giants' spot in the top eight as the rankings begin to take shape.

Fenerbahce will be lighter in defence than ideal without centre-backs Jayden Oosterwolde and Kojo Peprah Oppong, the former with a hamstring injury and the latter having been forced off against Goztepe.

Ex-Man City star Nathan Ake is also a doubt due to a muscle problem, so Archie Brown and Milan Skriniar could start at the heart of the hosts' defence, flanked by Mert Muldur and Munir Levent Mercan.

Elsewhere, attacking midfielder Marco Asensio was revealed to require knee surgery last month, though Mason Greenwood, Irfan Can Kahveci and Oguz Aydin should be ready to operate behind striker Romelu Lukaku.

As for Liverpool, the Reds were dealt a fresh blow on Tuesday with the news that Ryan Gravenberch will miss the game due to a heel injury.

Centre-back Giovanni Leoni remains sidelined as he closes in on a return from an anterior cruciate ligament injury, while right-back options Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong are out due to respective knee and hamstring injuries.

In their absence, Ronald Araujo could continue on the right of the back four, alongside Jeremy Jacquet, Virgil van Dijk and Kostas Tsimikas.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Lewis Koumas may come into the XI for striker Alexander Isak, with Hugo Ekitike working through his rehabilitation following the Achilles injury he suffered in April.

Ederson; Muldur, Brown, Skriniar, Mercan; Kante, Guendouzi; Greenwood, Kahveci, Aydin; Lukaku

Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Koumas

Fenerbahce have been in poor form lately, but they will be determined to deliver a competitive performance in front of an intense home crowd.

Liverpool should have enough to come out on top despite the pressure applied by their opponents, though they are unlikely to keep a clean sheet in Istanbul.

#1841. 'Why I'm here': Scott Parker sends message to West Ham fans in first words as new manager

West Ham have confirmed the appointment of Scott Parker as their new manager.

The former Hammers midfielder has quickly been appointed on a two-and-a-half year contract to succeed Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked on Monday following a disappointing start to the Championship season.

Parker had been out of work since leaving Burnley by mutual consent in April following confirmation of their relegation from the Premier League and is a second-tier promotion specialist, having previously led Bournemouth, Fulham and Burnley to the top-flight.

His two-decade playing career included a memorable four-year stint at West Ham between 2007-11, where he made 129 appearances across all competitions and won back-to-back Player of the Season awards after joining from Newcastle in a £7million move.

Parker - who also played for Chelsea and Charlton - eventually left for rivals Tottenham in 2011 after handing in a transfer request, staying at Spurs for two seasons before finishing his career at Fulham.

“It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a Club that means so much to me and my family,” Parker said. “A lot of very fond memories of my time here - four years of probably the best football I played in my career.

“There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn’t have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly.

#1839. Goalkeeper involved in Jesus de Miguel death 'is suffering' after incident

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono “is suffering” following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, says team-mate Lautaro Spatz.

Owono collided with De Miguel during a Spanish second-tier game on Monday, which saw the forward suffer a cardiac arrest and later die in hospital.

Equatorial Guinea international Owono, 25, has since received racist abuse on social media, with his Instagram account subsequently deactivated.

Spatz, who was on the pitch when the incident happened, said the FC Andorra squad remained in shock.

"The entire FC Andorra squad has been in shock, devastated and deeply affected by what has happened,” he wrote on Instagram.

“It is a tragedy that we could never have imagined experiencing on a football pitch.

"I would also like to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened.

"Those of us who know him are aware of the sort of person he is, how much he is suffering at this time, and that he would never have intended to harm anyone.

“In football, there are accidental incidents, but no one could have imagined that one of them could lead to such tragic consequences."

Spanish police have opened an investigation into De Miguel’s death, in accordance with procedures for deaths involving non-natural causes, including accidents.

Tenerife’s majority shareholder Rayco García confirmed the entire squad would travel to mainland Spain to attend De Miguel’s funeral in Navahermosa, Toledo, on Thursday.

García told El Larguero: "The important thing now is for the players to say goodbye to their teammate and come to terms with what has happened. It's a tragic situation. There are things that some of our players shouldn't have had to witness.

“A football pitch is a place where you're meant to have a good time, and what we saw was anything but that.

"We're still in shock. The entire squad is going to the funeral, without exception. Then we'll return to Tenerife. The players will have the day off to continue coming to terms with this terrible blow. And on Saturday, at the Heliodoro [stadium,] we plan to hold a lovely tribute in his memory.

"We want to start coming to terms with this as soon as possible and look to the future. We know that Jesús will be with us."

#1835. “I can’t change it” – Chivu looks back after three derby defeats to Milan

After last night’s win against Inter, AC Milan have now gone eight games without a defeat in the Derby della Madonnina.

In years gone by, the derby was a result to skip over for Milan. It was a defeat waiting to happen and it seemingly couldn’t be changed and then it flipped. Matteo Gabbia’s goal stopped the streak and in turn, it started a new one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri entered last night’s game with a run of seven unbeaten and they finished the night with eight unbeaten and a fourth consecutive win. It’s a first in itself for more than 50 years, which is telling.

It’s a result which brought Gerry Cardinale to tears and it’s clear that something has really clicked at San Siro, as the player ratings showed.

Speaking at a press conference after the game, as relayed by MilanNews, the Inter coach spoke about several things, including his unfavourable record in the Derby della Madonnina.

“Compared to last year, there’s something to note about our approach to matches: the superficiality and casualness with which we handle certain situations, where we lack a bit of grit, a bit of determination, a bit of danger perception. But we need to rediscover them.

“We need to be aware that right now, despite a few more points than last year, we’ve lost something that absolutely needs to be rediscovered.”

“I couldn’t, because the forwards have had some problems in the last few days. Bonny only made himself available on the last day after two days with a fever of 39°C and severe nausea and vomiting, so we were forced to find a solution, to make a virtue of necessity, changing the system a bit.

“We knew that, in this type of match, it would be the right thing to have pace on the wings with Spence and Carlos and attack the line a bit more, as well as looking for depth in space with Diouf operating under the striker, looking for both him and Sucic between the lines.

“Unfortunately, sometimes things don’t work out, but, I repeat, we were forced to change.”

“It’s too easy to talk now that Lautaro is injured and the other two forwards aren’t feeling well. These things happen, fortunately not often. We’ll make some assessments, but we’re still happy with our four forwards, in addition to what Lavelli gives us, what Mosconi gives us, and whoever we bring in from the Under 23s.

“But, I repeat, it’s too easy to bring these things up at a time when two forwards aren’t at their best and the third is injured.”

Is there something mental that comes into play in the derby?

“There’s always something mental, I think, and history teaches us this, when you get to play another season after winning.

“So, let’s try not to throw everything away and try to rediscover some determination, some humility in doing certain things, starting with myself, because I’m primarily responsible for everything we do.

“We shouldn’t throw everything away because we’ve reached the tenth matchday and this is the first game we’ve lost. We’ve got 25 points, and last year we’d got fewer, but we’ve always been able to react, we’ve always kept our feet on the ground and our heads down to build a strong season.

“That’s what we’d like to do again this year, because we have this desire and this ambition to have another strong season; we just need to find the way to build it again.”

By Ben Sully | 03 Nov 2026 00:12, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 03:56

Everton manager David Moyes has left the door open for Jack Grealish to reignite his career at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite being punished for a disciplinary issue.

Grealish, who is currently in his second loan spell from Manchester City, was left out of the squad for Thursday's 3-1 EFL Cup win over Newcastle United due to a disciplinary breach.

Reports suggested Grealish was punished after failing to show for a training session in the lead-up to the midweek fixture.

Grealish's name was once again absent when Everton published their teamsheet for Monday's Premier League away clash against Newcastle.

Explaining the attacker's latest absence, Everton published a short statement on their official X account: "Jack Grealish is not match fit and therefore not part of tonight’s squad."

The Toffees went on to claim a 1-0 victory at St James' Park, moving them up to seventh spot in the Premier League table.

Questioned about Grealish's absence after the win, Moyes told BBC Sport: "He's unavailable at the moment, and we will make a decision with the club when we think that availability comes back."

When asked whether his omission was fitness-related, the Everton boss said: "All I'm giving out is that he is unavailable at the moment."

In his post-match press conference, Moyes admitted he was unsure whether Grealish would be back in the squad for Friday's home clash against Coventry City.

However, he was able to offer a clearer response when asked if there is a chance for the 31-year-old to return, telling reporters: “Of course there is, yes."

The upcoming meeting against Frank Lampard's side represents Everton's final game before the international break.

#1833. Crystal Palace learn Jean-Philippe Mateta appeal verdict after Tottenham red card

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Crystal Palace have failed with their appeal against Jean-Philippe Mateta’s red card against Tottenham.

The French striker will serve a three-match suspension following his early dismissal during Saturday’s 2-0 loss in north London.

Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute for a lunging challenge on Tottenham captain Micky van de Ven, making contact with his ankle.

He was shown a straight red card by referee Michael Oliver following a VAR review, having initially only been booked, leaving struggling Palace to play most of the match against resurgent Spurs with 10 men.

Palace believed that the contact was accidental and launched an appeal in a bid to get Mateta’s ban overturned ahead of Sunday’s pivotal visit of Liverpool to Selhurst Park in the Premier League.

However, that has now been rejected by the Football Association (FA), meaning he will be absent against Liverpool and for the following two top-flight matches that take place after the November international break - against Coventry and Hull.

“An independent regulatory commission has dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment in relation to Jean-Philippe Mateta,” the FA said in a statement.

The suspension does not apply to European competition, so Mateta will be free to play in Palace’s upcoming Europa League games against Hoffenheim and Real Sociedad.

The 29-year-old has made five appearances across all competitions so far this term, scoring once and spending time out with a hamstring injury.

His latest absence in the Premier League is another huge blow for under-fire Eagles manager Pierre Sage, whose future at the club remains subject to severe scrutiny before facing Liverpool and heading into another international break.

#1831. Who are Scott Parker's backroom team? West Ham legends reunite for new era

West Ham have announced the appointment of Scott Parker as their new head coach to replace Nuno Espirito Santo.

Parker quickly succeeds Nuno, who was sacked on Tuesday morning after West Ham’s 3-1 defeat by West Brom, as the Irons look to get their automatic promotion bid back on track.

The former West Ham midfielder is seen as a safe pair of hands given his knowledge of the club and vast previous experience in getting teams promoted from the Championship.

West Ham are currently eighth in the Championship table, having won six of their first 13 league games, and take on Cardiff on Wednesday night, with Parker set to be in the dugout.

The 46-year-old, who has been out of work since leaving Burnley in April following confirmation of their relegation from the Premier League, will be joined by first-team coaches Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine, while Mark Noble will also be working closely with the squad.

The permanent structure of Parker’s backroom staff has yet to be announced, but Standard Sport has assessed who will assist the former England international during his first game at the helm in Wales.

A club legend and former team-mate of Parker’s, Noble became West Ham’s sporting director in January 2023 but now looks set for a more hands-on role within the backroom team.

It is unclear just what job Noble, who made 550 appearances for West Ham as a player, will undertake and where he will fit in as Parker looks to settle on a permanent backroom structure over the coming weeks.

Another former West Ham player with more than 500 appearances to his name, Potts was promoted from academy coach to Nuno’s backroom team in October 2025 after impressing on an interim basis following the Portuguese’s arrival at the club.

He helped bridge the gap between the club’s academy and the first team, with Nuno handing chances to youngsters such as Freddie Potts, Mohamadou Kante, Airidas Golambeckis and Ezra Mayers last season.

Prenderville worked in West Ham’s academy before being promoted to Nuno’s backroom team last season.

He was part of the Under-18s coaching team in 2022/23 when West Ham won the FA Youth Cup, beating Arsenal 5-1 at the Emirates Stadium. Prenderville has played an important role in the development of several academy-turned-first-team players.

A West Ham fan, Lepine was appointed head of academy goalkeeping in November 2020 before being promoted to Nuno’s backroom team.

He worked alongside Nuno’s long-time assistant, Rui Barbosa, as a goalkeeping coach and helped Mads Hermansen re-establish himself as the club’s first-choice option after he was dropped from the side under Graham Potter.

#1828. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners 'set sights' on Junior Kroupi swoop - but face competition from two Champions League clubs

By Ben Sully | 03 Nov 2026 01:05, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 02:50

Arsenal have reportedly earmarked Bournemouth star Junior Kroupi as a transfer target ahead of the January window.

The Gunners currently enjoy a three-point lead at the top of the Premier League table after winning eight of their nine matches this season.

Arsenal's league position is largely based on a strong backline that has recorded six clean sheets, the latest of which came in Sunday's hard-fought 1-0 win over Liverpool.

While their backline is their major strength, Arsenal can still improve at the opposite end of the pitch, which is an area Mikel Arteta is keen to address in the winter transfer window.

According to The Mirror, the Arsenal boss has made signing a 'top-class' striker his main priority for the winter market.

Arteta can currently call upon Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres as his main centre-forward options, but the latter has netted just once in 12 appearances this term and has been linked with a potential move away.

The report claims the Gunners have their sights on Bournemouth's Kroupi, although they will need to overcome some major obstacles to pull off the transfer in the new year.

Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain and German giants Bayern Munich are among those obstacles, with the European heavyweights believed to be among Kroupi's suitors.

Even if they can get ahead of their competition, Arsenal would still face the difficult task of convincing Bournemouth to part ways with an important player in the middle of the season.

Kroupi finished the 2025-26 Premier League season as Bournemouth's top scorer after netting 13 goals in 33 appearances.

The Frenchman's progress has been hampered by a foot injury which required surgery and forced him to miss the first two months of the season.

Kroupi has recently returned to the fray with three substitute appearances, although Bournemouth boss Marco Rose is keen to exercise caution with the minutes he gives the 20-year-old as he continues to build up fitness.

With Kroupi being eased back into action, Bournemouth will be reluctant to sanction his departure in January, especially as they will want to keep their key players to give them the best chance of enjoying success this term.

The Cherries harbour ambitions of going a long way in the Europa League, while they are also looking to match or go close to equalling last season's sixth-place finish in the Premier League.

#1826. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: ‘We have no fear at all’, Pau Torres identifies Barca weakness

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 06:55, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 07:08

Barcelona have been through a run of tricky games, losing their 100% record in the Champions League and La Liga to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, and now, after recovering with two wins, they face another big challenge. On Tuesday, Barcelona host Aston Villa at the Camp Nou.

The English side have won every game in the European competition and are unbeaten in five Premier League matches. That is why Pau Torres, an undisputed starter for Aston Villa, is not afraid at all of the game against Barcelona.

‘We have no fear at all, but we do have respect. We know how difficult it will be, but nothing is impossible. We will try to compete with our own weapons’ - he said in an interview with Catalan newspaper Sport.

The 29-year-old defender also pointed out what to exploit in the contest.

Barcelona, under the management of Hansi Flick, are characterised by heavy pressing in the attacking half, which forces a high defensive line to keep up with the rest of the team. That space is something for Aston Villa to exploit, as Pau Torres explained, based on the profile of their trio of very quick attackers, including a Brazilian.

‘This year we have very vertical players, such as Ibrahim Mbaye, Alysson and Nicolas Jackson himself. They work very well when opponents leave space behind the defence.’

Of course, there is a way to attack, but for more than 60% of the time Barcelona’s opponents will be defending. Focus is a must if they are to avoid conceding against Barcelona, who have scored 57 times in 14 matches this season. ‘If we want to get a positive result, we will have to be alert defensively.’

Pau Torres also has a special mission. As a left-sided centre-back, he could come up against right winger Lamine Yamal several times because of the cover he will have to provide for left-back Ian Maatsen, who is known for being very attacking.

‘When you play this type of match, you always want to face the best to find out what level you are at. It will be a pleasure to play against Lamine and have to mark him on some occasions.

He always surprises, he is unpredictable and, often, just one player to mark him is not enough. We will have to be very alert to the cover from team-mates.’

The clash, which promises to be an interesting one, kicks off at 8pm UK time on Tuesday. Aston Villa share top spot in the Champions League league phase with Paris Saint-Germain, who are ahead on goals scored, Liverpool, Real Madrid and Real Betis. Barcelona are looking to recover after losing 4-2 to leaders Paris Saint-Germain in the last round.

#1824. Mikel Arteta has Max Dowman conundrum to solve as Arsenal face Prague battle

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Prague will always hold a special place in Max Dowman's heart.

Aged 15 years and 308 days old, Dowman came on at the Fortuna Arena last season and in doing so became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League.

UEFA have been kind enough to mark the anniversary. Exactly a year on from that fixture, Arsenal are back at the same stadium to face Slavia Prague once again.

It has been an eventful 12 months for Dowman, who now has a Premier League medal in his possession, but it has been a particularly dramatic week.

The 16-year-old has served the first match of a three-game suspension for the straight red card he was shown against Fleetwood.

That ban does not apply to European competitions. Dowman played a full part in training on Tuesday and is part of the travelling squad in Prague.

The decision for Mikel Arteta is whether to hand Dowman a first Champions League start, or continue a period of tough love.

In response to criticism of his reaction to Dowman at Fleetwood, when he angrily spoke to the teenager as he walked off the pitch, Arteta made it clear that no allowances would be made for Dowman because of his age.

“This is the environment and this is the reality,” Arteta said.

“Otherwise we are in Disneyland, we are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine.

“But at the same time we are going to demand him, like to anybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play.”

Dowman cannot play in the Premier League until Arsenal host Manchester City on November 29, but the Champions League offers the chance for him to move on from that red card.

It was the second time in a month that Dowman had been sent off, having also been dismissed for England's Under-19s.

Arteta has been very clear that he has hammered home the message to Dowman that he must expect rough treatment and, more importantly, that he cannot react.

Those discussions will have continued since the Fleetwood red card and those thoughts will be front of Arteta's mind when he selects his lineup in Prague.

Before Tuesday night's fixtures in the Champions League, Slavia Prague ranked seventh out of the 36 teams in the competition for fouls committed. They are the only side to have been shown two red cards this season.

When the two teams met last season, the hosts committed 24 fouls. Dowman was barely on the pitch for 20 minutes and was fouled twice.

The approach Slavia Prague might adopt towards Dowman, then, is no great surprise. Particularly after his recent red cards, there will be a feeling that the teenager can be riled and will react to a physical test.

However, Arsenal are not flush with options. Bukayo Saka is out with a quad injury and Noni Madueke just about shook off an ankle issue in time to play the full 90 minutes at Anfield.

With Saka out, Madueke is a pivotal part of Arsenal's attack and they cannot afford for him to be injured. Dowman is now unable to ease the domestic load but he can allow Madueke a precious rest on Wednesday night.

Ordinarily, that would feel like a fairly obvious call for Arteta to make. The past week has perhaps complicated the situation and given Arteta more to ponder.

Does he leave Dowman on the bench, whether it be to send him a message or to protect him considering the current spotlight? Or does he show his faith in the teenager and trust him to learn the necessary lessons to keep a cooler head?

Arteta indicated at his pre-match press conference that he will opt for the latter and put the Fleetwood saga in the past.

“That’s a chapter that is gone,” Arteta said.

“It’s a moment of learning for all of us and we move on. You learn from the not so good ones, make sure you learn from the great ones as well. He’s been in great spirits.”

Against limited opposition and on a night where rotation is likely, it feels an ideal opportunity for Arteta to showcase his trust and Dowman to repay it.

#1823. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.
